  - Explanation: Boundary data and individual edge-count inputs yield the full simultaneous pre-stack contract with constants fixed before final guards, resolution and weights.
- **claim-ambient-weak-costs** (bound, [source](#stmt-ha-ambient-tests)): With the preceding geometry and local weights fixed, the ordinary weak costs are controlled by the carrier budgets with constant $C_{\mathrm w}$, plus freely small absolute errors. The control is uniform over meshes sufficiently fine for prescribed buffer and guard requirements. It applies simultaneously to the exterior residual, the full-rank correction shells, and the marked collars weighted by $\ell_U/d_U$.
  - Explanation: Weighted coarea and ambient edge-density estimates charge ordinary derivative costs to the carrier’s preassigned regional budgets uniformly under sufficiently fine refinement.
- **claim-sharp-counts-and-discarded-costs** (bound, [source](#stmt-ha-sharp-counts)): The meshes and the subsequent stratified samples can be chosen so that the sharp-template count conditions hold outside tetrahedra of arbitrarily small aggregate pre-derivative $p$-cost. More precisely, for the two family counts on an edge $l$, $$\label{ha:sharp-edge} \frac{N_{l,i}W}{H} \le (1+C(\zeta+c_*)) \left\|(BV)_i\frac{\Delta y_l}{H}\right\|+e_l, \qquad e_l\ge0,$$ and the aggregate $\sum_lH^3e_l^p$ can be arbitrarily small after all fixed template, transition and physical conversion factors. The dirty portions left by Proposition <a href="#ms:sharp-contract" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ms:sharp-contract">62</a> have arbitrarily small aggregate evaluated pre-derivative $p$-cost in aligned coordinates.
  - Explanation: Affine directional comparisons, stratified sampling and convolution control make nonregular, high-leakage and dirty contributions arbitrarily affordable.
- **claim-prior-capacities-and-simultaneous-selection** (construction, [source](#stmt-ha-capacities)): For each member of a locally finite family of buffered compact barrier charts one can fix a finite capacity $A_j$, independently of guard spacing and final mesh resolution. After fixing these capacities, one can choose the guards, mesh and samples so that substitution of the selected edge counts into the slope bounds of Proposition <a href="#ms:prestacks" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ms:prestacks">63</a> gives local integral upper budgets at most $A_j$. The same data meet the weak aggregate bounds of Lemma <a href="#ha:ambient-tests" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ha:ambient-tests">64</a> and the sharp count and discarded-cost bounds of Lemma <a href="#ha:sharp-counts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ha:sharp-counts">65</a>.
  - Explanation: Uniform expected count-based budgets fix capacities before guards; a joint admissible choice then satisfies capacities and the weak and sharp objectives.
- **claim-initial-walls-with-selected-budgets** (construction, [source](#stmt-ha-initial-walls)): The guards, mesh, samples and count bounds selected in Lemma <a href="#ha:capacities" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ha:capacities">66</a> admit pre-stacks satisfying Definition <a href="#wl:prestack" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="wl:prestack">32</a> and avoiding the selected guards. Their actual slope majorant $G$ satisfies $$\int_{U_j}G^p\le A_j$$ on every buffered barrier chart $U_j$, together with the weak and sharp estimates of Lemmas <a href="#ha:ambient-tests" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ha:ambient-tests">64</a> and <a href="#ha:sharp-counts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ha:sharp-counts">65</a>. The mesh and samples are unchanged. Consequently the hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#wl:realization" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="wl:realization">41</a> hold.
  - Explanation: A common carrier opening followed by boundary preparation and separate-colour normalization realizes the selected counts as actual guard-avoiding pre-stacks.
- **claim-physical-gradient-saturation** (bound, [source](#stmt-ha-saturation)): On the union of the saturation interiors, $$\label{ha:physical-saturation} \int \|D(P_0Th)-Df\|^p \le C_p(\eta+\gamma)(1+E) +\text{freely small errors}.$$ The constant in the displayed leading term is independent of the compact jet and chart bounds.
  - Explanation: Nearly sharp scalar energy and pinned mean gradients give strong gradient accuracy. Source and target scale cancellation keeps the leading constant independent of compact jet bounds.
- **claim-strong-smoothing-of-local-bilip-maps** (theorem, [source](#stmt-sm-smoothing)): Let $\Omega,\Omega'\subset\mathbb R^3$ be bounded domains, let $1\le p<\infty$, and let $H:\Omega\to\Omega'$ be a locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism in $W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ and every continuous function $\xi:\Omega\to(0,\infty)$, there is a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $g:\Omega\to\Omega'$ such that $$\label{sm:smoothing-conclusion} \left\lVert g-H\right\rVert_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}<\varepsilon, \qquad \|g(x)-H(x)\|<\xi(x)\quad(x\in\Omega).$$ In particular, $g$ belongs to $W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, and the approximations have exactly the target $\Omega'$.
  - Explanation: A locally bi-Lipschitz Sobolev homeomorphism admits smooth diffeomorphic approximation with strong Sobolev error and arbitrary positive continuous pointwise value tolerance.
- **claim-fine-relative-pl-approximation** (construction, [source](#stmt-sm-relative-pl)): Let $M,N$ be PL three-manifolds without boundary, with $N$ metrized, and let $f:M\to N$ be a homeomorphism. Suppose that $K\subset M$ is closed and that $f$ is PL on an open neighborhood of $K$. Given a continuous function $\eta:M\to(0,\infty)$, there is a PL homeomorphism $f_1:M\to N$ which agrees with $f$ on a neighborhood of $K$ and satisfies $$d_N(f_1(x),f(x))<\eta(x)\qquad(x\in M).$$ Noncompact manifolds are allowed. For manifolds with boundary the same statement holds if $K$ contains $\partial M$ and $f$ is PL near $K$.
  - Explanation: Qualitative relative topology gives fine PL homeomorphic approximation while fixing a neighborhood where the original map is already PL.
- **claim-small-local-ambient-extension** (construction, [source](#stmt-sm-local-extension)): Fix a closed Euclidean cube $B\subset\mathbb R^3$, compact sets $C,D\subset B$ with $C\subset\operatorname{int}B$, and an open neighborhood $O$ of $C\cup D\cup\partial B$. For every $\lambda>0$ there is a $\delta>0$, depending only on these source sets and on $\lambda$, with the following property. If $e:O\to\mathbb R^3$ is an embedding, $$\sup_{x\in O}\|e(x)-x\|<\delta, \qquad e=\operatorname{id}\ \hbox{on }D\cup\partial B,$$ then there is a homeomorphism $A:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ such that $$\label{sm:extension-conclusion} A=e\ \hbox{on }C,\qquad A=\operatorname{id}\ \hbox{on }D\cup(\mathbb R^3\setminus\operatorname{int}B), \qquad \sup_{\mathbb R^3}\|A-\operatorname{id}\|<\lambda.$$ The number $\delta$ is uniform over a finite list of fixed normalized configurations $(B,C,D,O)$. No derivative bound on $e$ is required.
  - Explanation: A sufficiently small embedding extends to an ambient homeomorphism supported in the cube and fixing protected sets; no derivative estimate is required.
- **claim-fine-proper-degree-target-control** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-sm-proper-degree)): Let $h:\Omega\to\Omega'$ be an orientation-preserving homeomorphism between bounded domains, and let $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ be a smooth map with $\det Dg>0$. If $$\label{sm:target-distance} \|g(x)-h(x)\|<\frac12\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(h(x),\mathbb R^3\setminus\Omega') \qquad(x\in\Omega),$$ then $g$ is a diffeomorphism of $\Omega$ onto $\Omega'$.
  - Explanation: Positive local degree and the boundary-distance value condition give a proper degree-one map, hence a diffeomorphism onto the original target.
- **claim-strong-pl-smoothing** (theorem, [source](#stmt-sm-pl-smoothing)): The conclusion of Theorem <a href="#sm:smoothing" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sm:smoothing">70</a> holds if $H$ is replaced by a locally finite PL homeomorphism $h:\Omega\to\Omega'$ in $W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$.
  - Explanation: Locally finite PL homeomorphisms have the same strong smoothing and fine value conclusion as the locally bi-Lipschitz smoothing theorem.
- **claim-adapted-dyadic-meshes** (construction, [source](#stmt-sm-mesh)): There is an absolute integer $n_0$ with the following property. Given arbitrary positive local upper bounds on the fine scale, there is a locally finite dyadic cube decomposition $\mathcal Q$ of $\Omega$ with centers $c_Q$ and side lengths $l_Q$ for which, on writing $$\label{sm:patch-box} B_Q(s)=c_Q+[-s l_Q,s l_Q]^3,$$ the following hold:* 1. *$B_Q(100)\Subset\Omega$, and cubes meeting $B_Q(50)$ have side lengths comparable to $l_Q$ by absolute constants.* 2. *The normalized cube configurations in $B_Q(6)$ belong to a finite list. There is a conforming affine triangulation of $\mathcal Q$ with finitely many normalized nondegenerate shapes on these configurations.* 3. *The cubes have $n_0$ colors so that the closed boxes $B_Q(6)$ of a single color are pairwise disjoint.* 4. *Attach to $Q$ a coarse index $P(Q)$ containing $c_Q$, using a fixed convention on coarse boundaries. The initial scale bounds can be reduced so that all interactions through any fixed number of neighboring patch layers are confined to a fixed locally finite graph of coarse indices, independent of further mesh refinement. The corresponding patches lie in the neighborhoods on which the required bounds in Equation <a href="#sm:coarse-bilip" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="sm:coarse-bilip">[sm:coarse-bilip]</a> hold.* *The upper bounds on the fine scale remain arbitrarily prescribable.
  - Explanation: An arbitrarily fine adapted dyadic decomposition has finite normalized configurations, conforming shape lists, disjoint colour classes and resolution-independent coarse interactions.
- **claim-protected-core-insertion** (construction, [source](#stmt-sm-insertion)): Consider a patch $Q$ and a finite collection of older protected boxes with the relative sizes and positions provided by Lemma <a href="#sm:mesh" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sm:mesh">75</a>. For every older box prescribe a larger half-shrunk box and a smaller fully-shrunk box, separated by a fixed positive normalized margin. Let $G:\Omega\to\Omega'$ be a homeomorphism, and let $h_Q$ be a PL embedding on a neighborhood of $B_Q(3)$. Assume that $h_Q=G$ on the overlaps with the half-shrunk boxes.* *For every $\lambda>0$ there is an $a>0$, depending only on $\lambda$, the normalized source configuration, and a local constant $K_P$ in Equation <a href="#sm:coarse-bilip" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="sm:coarse-bilip">[sm:coarse-bilip]</a>, such that $$\label{sm:insertion-smallness} \sup_{B_Q(5)}\|G-H\|<a l_Q, \qquad \sup_{B_Q(3)}\|h_Q-H\|<a l_Q$$ implies the following conclusion. There is a domain homeomorphism $A$ supported in $B_Q(5)$, with $$\sup\|A-\operatorname{id}\|<\lambda l_Q,$$ such that $G\circ A=h_Q$ on a neighborhood of $B_Q(2)$ and $G\circ A=G$ on the fully-shrunk older boxes. The tolerances are uniform over a finite list of source configurations. They do not depend on the derivatives of $G$ or of $h_Q$.
  - Explanation: Value closeness to the reference map permits local PL insertion by a small domain homeomorphism while preserving fully shrunken older cores.
- **claim-strong-pl-approximation-of-local-bilip-maps** (theorem, [source](#stmt-sm-bilip-pl)): Under the hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#sm:smoothing" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sm:smoothing">70</a>, there is a locally finite PL homeomorphism $G:\Omega\to\Omega'$ satisfying $$\left\lVert G-H\right\rVert_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}<\varepsilon, \qquad \|G(x)-H(x)\|<\xi(x)\quad(x\in\Omega).$$
  - Explanation: Finite normalized PL libraries fix local derivative bounds before the bad-cube measure is reduced, yielding strong PL approximation with the exact target.

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-hp-flattening",
        "exact_quote": "Given $\\varepsilon>0$, $0<\\lambda<1/100$, and a positive continuous fine tolerance $a$ on $\\Lambda$, one can retain a compact set $K\\subset D$ with $\\mu(D\\setminus K)<\\varepsilon$ and construct a Lipschitz map $S_0:\\Lambda\\to\\Lambda$ with the following properties.*\n\n1.  *The map is the identity outside finitely many disjoint rectangular boxes compactly contained in $\\Lambda$, $\\mathop{\\mathrm{Lip}}(S_0)\\le C$, and $|S_0(y)-y|<a(y)$. The constant $C$ is absolute. For $0<\\kappa\\le1$, $$S_\\kappa=(1-\\kappa)S_0+\\kappa\\operatorname{id}$$ is a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism of $\\Lambda$ onto itself.*\n\n\n2.  *With $F_\\kappa=S_\\kappa\\circ f$ for $0\\le\\kappa\\le1$, $$\\label{hp:flattening-derivative}\n     |DF_\\kappa|\\le C|Df|\\quad\\hbox{a.e. on }\\Omega,\n     \\qquad\n     |DF_\\kappa-Df|\\le C\\lambda|Df|\n                       \\quad\\hbox{a.e. on }K.$$ Moreover, $F_\\kappa\\to F_0$ strongly in $W^{1,p}(\\Omega;\\mathbb R^3)$, and $\\mathop{\\mathrm{rank}}DF_0=\\mathop{\\mathrm{rank}}Df$ almost everywhere on $K$.*\n\n3.  *The compact set $F_0(K)$ is contained in finitely many compact flat plate patches with pairwise disjoint ambient neighborhoods. Each patch lies in a plane of slope at most $C\\lambda$ in one of the chosen coordinates. Each patch has an assigned rank, either one or two; the rank-one patches can in addition retain any prescribed small directional grouping of $\\operatorname{im}Df$.*\n\n\n4.  *There is a compact zero-volume set $Z\\Subset\\Lambda$, contained in finitely many piecewise affine graph sheets, such that $$\\label{hp:flattening-homeomorphic-complement}\n     S_0:\\Lambda\\setminus S_0^{-1}(Z)\\longrightarrow\\Lambda\\setminus Z$$ is a locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism. Its only non-singleton fibres are the collapsed vertical intervals over points of $Z$. Consequently $F_0$ is a homeomorphism from $\\Omega\\setminus F_0^{-1}(Z)$ onto $\\Lambda\\setminus Z$.*\n\n*For almost every target point outside $Z$, its unique preimage under this last homeomorphism either is a regular point of $F_0$ with positive invertible differential and the power-mean test in <a href=\"#hp:regular-point-tests\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"hp:regular-point-tests\">[hp:regular-point-tests]</a>, or belongs to a fixed source null set. When $p\\ge3$, the second alternative occurs only on a target null set.",
        "source_id": "PM-368.2"
      },

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-hp-wells",
        "exact_quote": "Let finitely many separated compact pieces of the retained $F_0$-image lie on flat plates, with relatively compact disjoint ambient chart neighborhoods. Let a positive continuous motion scale $\\delta$ on $\\Lambda$ be prescribed. After an arbitrarily small $\\mu$-loss, one can choose, on each plate, an origin $z$, a unit vector $n$ as close as desired to its normal, a number $d>0$, and nested protected horizontal rectangles in $n^\\perp$ with the following properties. There is a nonnegative smooth compactly supported function $b_1$ on $\\Lambda$, extended by zero to $\\mathbb R^3$, such that*\n\n1.  *$\\Delta b_1\\leq C$ with an absolute constant, and $b_1$ is as small as prescribed relative to $\\delta^2$. In particular $b_1=o(\\mathop{\\mathrm{dist}}(\\cdot,\\mathbb R^3\\setminus\\Lambda)^2)$ at the boundary.*\n\n\n2.  *For every $h$ in a protected horizontal rectangle, put $q=z+h$. The affine function $$L_h(x)=q\\cdot x-\\tfrac12|q|^2+d^2$$ supports $\\psi_1(x)=|x|^2/2+b_1(x)$ globally, and its contact set consists exactly of $q+dn$ and $q-dn$. In particular, $$\\label{hp:paired-dual-value}\n     \\sup_x\\{q\\cdot x-\\psi_1(x)\\}=\\tfrac12|q|^2-d^2.$$ For a fixed compact rectangle and any fixed neighborhoods of these two endpoint sheets, the supporting gap is uniformly positive outside the neighborhoods.*\n\n\n3.  *The assigned central data $X=F_0(x)$ have $|\\langle X-z,n\\rangle|<d/4$. For almost every assigned $x$ with respect to $\\mu$, both points $$\\label{hp:sampled-endpoints}\n     Y_\\pm(X)=X+n\\bigl(\\pm d-\\langle X-z,n\\rangle\\bigr)$$ belong to genuine homeomorphic target neighborhoods of $F_0$ and have either a regular full-rank inverse point or an inverse point in a fixed source null set. The latter alternative is needed only when $2<p<3$.*\n\n*All assertions persist after shrinking the protected horizontal rectangles. The endpoint assignments can be restricted to compact sets on which their inverse points and their regular or exceptional types have fixed separated compact ranges.",

      },

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-hp-immersed-skeleton",
        "exact_quote": "There are positive constants $b,C_0,C_1$ and, for every sufficiently small dyadic $s$, a locally finite conforming triangulation $\\mathcal T_s$ of $\\{0<t<2s\\}$ with the following properties. If $D\\in\\mathcal T_s$ has scale $\\ell_D$, then $$\\mathop{\\mathrm{diam}}D\\asymp\\ell_D,\n \\qquad \\ell_D\\asymp\\min\\{s,t(x)\\}\\quad(x\\in D),$$ where the second assertion allows the uniform constants implicit in $\\asymp$. The simplices have uniformly controlled shapes and finitely many local configurations up to translation and rescaling. There is a smooth orientation-preserving local diffeomorphism $i$ on an open neighborhood $\\mathcal U$ of their two-skeleton, including a neighborhood of the outer boundary $\\{t=2s\\}$, such that $$i=\\operatorname{id}\\text{ near }\\{t=2s\\},\\qquad\n |i(x)-x|\\leq C_0s.$$ The neighborhood contains, at every simplex, a neighborhood of its skeleton of width $b\\ell_D$. On a slightly smaller such neighborhood, $$\\label{hp:immersion-bounds}\n |Di|\\leq C_1\\frac{s}{\\ell_D},\\qquad\n |(Di)^{-1}|\\leq C_1\\frac{\\ell_D}{s},\\qquad\n |D^2i|\\leq C_1\\frac{s}{\\ell_D^2}.$$ There are also uniform local inverse charts: a chart centered at a point of the smaller neighborhood contains a source ball of radius $b_1\\ell_D$, and its image contains the corresponding target ball of radius $b_2s$, for fixed $b_1,b_2>0$.*\n\n\n*More precisely, after splitting into a bounded number of charts per simplex, the formulas for $i$ have the form $$\\label{hp:immersion-template}\n i(x_*+\\ell\\xi)=y_*+sI(\\xi),$$ where $I$ belongs to a fixed finite list of smooth formulas on fixed compact chart neighborhoods, and $y_*$ belongs to a fixed rational subdivision of the $s$-grid. For fixed $s$ there are only finitely many possible $y_*$ in the bounded region used by this construction. The map $i$ is permitted to have overlaps between different local charts.",

      },

        "anchor": "stmt-hp-cutoff",
        "exact_quote": "There are constants $C>2$ and $c>0$ with the following property. Let $1\\leq p<\\infty$, let $s$ be sufficiently small and dyadic, and let $h$ be a homeomorphism on an open neighborhood of $\\overline{B_{Cs}}$, onto its image, with $h\\in W^{1,p}_{\\mathrm{loc}}$. Suppose that $$\\label{hp:cutoff-closeness}\n |h(x)-x|\\leq cs\\qquad\\text{whenever }|t(x)|\\leq Cs.$$ One can replace $h$ inside $B_{2s}$ by a continuous Sobolev map $F$, keeping a neighborhood of its boundary unchanged, so that $$\\begin{aligned}\n &F=\\operatorname{id}\\quad\\text{on }B,\n \\qquad F(B_{2s})=h(B_{2s}),\\label{hp:cutoff-image}\\\\\n &\\int_{0<t<2s}|DF|^p\n \\leq C_p\\int_{|t|\\leq Cs}|Dh|^p.\\label{hp:cutoff-energy}\n\\end{aligned}$$ The only nonsingleton fibers of $F$ are tame closed balls over a countable set of target points. Their diameters tend to zero at every accumulation, and those target points can accumulate only on $\\partial B$. These fibers can be opened simultaneously to give a homeomorphism, altering $F$ only over arbitrarily small mutually disjoint target neighborhoods of their values. This last assertion is topological; it does not assert a Sobolev energy bound for the opened maps. If $h$ has volume Lusin property $N$, then so does $F$.",
        "source_id": "PM-368.2"
      },

        "anchor": "stmt-hp-opening",
        "exact_quote": "Let $F:\\Omega\\to\\Lambda$ be a continuous proper onto map obtained by locally finite image-preserving applications of Lemma <a href=\"#hp:cutoff\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"hp:cutoff\">11</a> in genuine homeomorphic neighborhoods. Assume that subsequent applications avoid earlier fibre values and their accumulation sets. Let $P$ be the countable set of non-singleton fibre values. Then its fibres are tame closed balls, form a null family on compact localizations, and their value accumulations have singleton fibres.         "anchor": "stmt-hp-exceptional-boxes",
        "exact_quote": "Let $E$ be a compact source null set contained in finitely many genuine homeomorphic neighborhoods of a continuous $W^{1,p}_{\\rm loc}$ map $F$, where $p>2$. Let $\\sigma$ be a finite measure supported on $E$, and let $g\\in L^1_{\\rm loc}$ be nonnegative. For any $a,b>0$, any prescribed source and target size bounds, and any closed sets separated from $E$, one can choose finitely many cubes $U$ with disjoint closures, avoiding those closed sets and compact in the given neighborhoods, such that, after a $\\sigma$-loss less than $a$, the retained data lie with positive prescribed relative margins in their interiors and $$\\label{hp:exceptional-cube-budget}\n \\int_{\\bigcup U^+}g< b,\n \\qquad\n \\sum_U\\ell_U\\int_{\\partial U}^{\\rm ext}g\\,d\\mathcal H^2<b.$$ Here $U^+$ are sufficiently small enlarged neighborhoods, and the superscript $\\rm ext$ means that each facet is allowed a fixed small tangential extension. The facet positions can be chosen to be $L^1$ Lebesgue points in their normal variable, and their $F$-images have zero three-dimensional volume. The relative insets and the further margins may be prescribed arbitrarily small before the final grid phase is selected.",

        "anchor": "stmt-hp-regular-implant",
        "exact_quote": "Let $F$ be a positively oriented $W^{1,p}_{\\rm loc}$ homeomorphism on a neighborhood of a compact set of regular full-rank source points. Suppose its jets and inverse jets are bounded there and its Fréchet and power-mean differentiation tests hold uniformly below a fixed radius. In sufficiently small target grid boxes one can implant exact positive affine cores, with arbitrarily small relative grid margins and with disjoint enlarged source comparison boxes. For a box of target side $R$ using the affine jet $b$ at one of its assigned inverse points, the new energy in its source support is at most $$\\label{hp:regular-implant-cost}\n C_p\\frac{|Db|^pR^3}{\\det Db}\n \\leq C_p\\int_{V_b}|DF|^p,$$ where $V_b$ is the source comparison box obtained as the affine preimage of a buffered target box. The constant depends only on $p$ and the fixed cubical cutoff construction, not on the condition number of $Db$. The choices may be made relative to previously fixed disjoint compact sets and exact cores.",

      },

    {
      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-hp-carrier",
        "exact_quote": "Prescribe a positive continuous source value tolerance $a:\\Omega\\to(0,\\infty)$ before applying Proposition <a href=\"#hp:flattening\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"hp:flattening\">8</a>. Use there a target tolerance $a_\\Lambda$ satisfying $$a_\\Lambda(y)\\leq\\tfrac14 a(f^{-1}(y)),$$ and then fix the resulting rank data and endpoint protections of Lemma <a href=\"#hp:wells\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"hp:wells\">9</a>. Fix also an enlargement factor $A>1$ for the marked collars, before assigning their facet budgets, and let $\\varepsilon>0$. After a total $\\mu$-loss smaller than $\\varepsilon$, a first round of choices gives $\\kappa>0$, a compact retained source set $K$, a continuous proper onto carrier $F_b^1:\\Omega\\to\\Lambda$, an exact open target set $O_1$, and compact endpoint rectangles strictly inside $O_1$. These choices precede any prescribed residual-volume thresholds. Fix a locally finite target Whitney tiling $\\mathcal Q$, and choose arbitrary numbers $a_Q>0$ for $Q\\in\\mathcal Q$, after $O_1$ and the endpoint buffers have been determined. A second round gives $F_b:\\Omega\\to\\Lambda$ and $O\\supset O_1$ such that:*\n\n1.  *$F_b$ is continuous, proper and onto, belongs to $W^{1,p}_{\\rm loc}$, and has only the countable tame ball fibres of Lemma <a href=\"#hp:opening\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"hp:opening\">12</a>. It is a genuine homeomorphism on target neighborhoods away from their values and accumulation seams. For $p\\geq3$ it satisfies volume Lusin $N$.*\n\n\n2.  *$O$ is a locally finite union of exact affine or PL core images. Every compact subset of such a core has a neighborhood on which $F_b$ and its inverse are exactly those of its affine or PL chart. In particular no point of $O$ has a nontrivial fibre, and $$\\label{hp:residual-volume}\n     \\mathcal L^3(Q\\setminus O)<a_Q\\qquad(Q\\in\\mathcal Q).$$ The compact endpoint rectangles retain their fixed buffers in $O_1$.*\n\n3.  *$F_b=F_\\kappa$ on a neighborhood of $K$. It meets the prescribed fine value tolerance relative to $f$. The choices of $\\kappa$ and of the retained central margins ensure that $F_\\kappa(K)$ stays in the protected central plate neighborhoods.*\n\n\n4.  *When $2<p<3$, there is a locally finite family of marked source cubes $U$ with disjoint closures, away from $K$, such that $$\\label{hp:small-marked-mass}\n     \\int_{\\bigcup U}(1+|Df|^p)<\\varepsilon.$$ For $p\\geq3$ this family is empty. Off the marked cubes the energy has the universal buffered regional estimate described below.*\n\n\n5.  *Write $C_U(w)$ for a cube-radius collar of physical width $w$ about $\\partial U$. For the prescribed enlargement factor $A$, the widths $w_U>0$ can be chosen after both rounds, with disjoint enlarged marked cubes, so that $$\\label{hp:marked-collar-budget}\n     \\sum_U\\frac{\\ell_U}{w_U}\n                 \\int_{C_U(Aw_U)}|DF_b|^p<\\varepsilon.$$ The same bound, multiplied by the $p$th power of the Lipschitz constant, holds after a uniformly Lipschitz output composition. The enlarged cubes may still have original $(1+|Df|^p)$-mass less than $2\\varepsilon$.*\n\n\n*The regional estimate in <span class=\"upright\">(iv)</span> has the following meaning. Suppose a locally finite family of regional tests $A_j$ and two successive small open buffered enlargements $A_j^{[1]}$ and $A_j^{[2]}$ are prescribed before the implants are made. All implants may be chosen so fine that $$\\label{hp:regional-energy}\n \\int_{A_j\\setminus\\bigcup U}|DF_b|^p\n       \\leq C_p\\int_{A_j^{[2]}}|Df|^p\n       \\qquad\\hbox{for every }j.$$ Here each enlargement has positive local buffer, the supports and comparison boxes meeting $A_j$ fit inside its first enlargement at the corresponding round, and $C_p$ is independent of all selected jet condition numbers, residual thresholds, and PL reference-map constants. In particular the tests may be reserved full-rank cut shells or ordinary regions outside prescribed interiors. The same construction works for summably weighted such tests toward the ends of the open domains.",
        "source_id": "PM-368.2"
      },

For the prescribed enlargement factor $A$, the widths $w_U>0$ can be chosen after both rounds, with disjoint enlarged marked cubes, so that $$\\label{hp:marked-collar-budget}\n     \\sum_U\\frac{\\ell_U}{w_U}\n                 \\int_{C_U(Aw_U)}|DF_b|^p<\\varepsilon.$$ The same bound, multiplied by the $p$th power of the Lipschitz constant, holds after a uniformly Lipschitz output composition. The enlarged cubes may still have original $(1+|Df|^p)$-mass less than $2\\varepsilon$.*\n\n\n*The regional estimate in <span class=\"upright\">(iv)</span> has the following meaning. Suppose a locally finite family of regional tests $A_j$ and two successive small open buffered enlargements $A_j^{[1]}$ and $A_j^{[2]}$ are prescribed before the implants are made. All implants may be chosen so fine that $$\\label{hp:regional-energy}\n \\int_{A_j\\setminus\\bigcup U}|DF_b|^p\n       \\leq C_p\\int_{A_j^{[2]}}|Df|^p\n       \\qquad\\hbox{for every }j.$$ Here each enlargement has positive local buffer, the supports and comparison boxes meeting $A_j$ fit inside its first enlargement at the corresponding round, and $C_p$ is independent of all selected jet condition numbers, residual thresholds, and PL reference-map constants.       "exact_statement": "Prescribe a positive continuous source value tolerance $a:\\Omega\\to(0,\\infty)$ before applying Proposition <a href=\"#hp:flattening\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"hp:flattening\">8</a>. Use there a target tolerance $a_\\Lambda$ satisfying $$a_\\Lambda(y)\\leq\\tfrac14 a(f^{-1}(y)),$$ and then fix the resulting rank data and endpoint protections of Lemma <a href=\"#hp:wells\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"hp:wells\">9</a>. Fix also an enlargement factor $A>1$ for the marked collars, before assigning their facet budgets, and let $\\varepsilon>0$. After a total $\\mu$-loss smaller than $\\varepsilon$, a first round of choices gives $\\kappa>0$, a compact retained source set $K$, a continuous proper onto carrier $F_b^1:\\Omega\\to\\Lambda$, an exact open target set $O_1$, and compact endpoint rectangles strictly inside $O_1$. These choices precede any prescribed residual-volume thresholds. Fix a locally finite target Whitney tiling $\\mathcal Q$, and choose arbitrary numbers $a_Q>0$ for $Q\\in\\mathcal Q$, after $O_1$ and the endpoint buffers have been determined. A second round gives $F_b:\\Omega\\to\\Lambda$ and $O\\supset O_1$ such that:*\n\n1.  *$F_b$ is continuous, proper and onto, belongs to $W^{1,p}_{\\rm loc}$, and has only the countable tame ball fibres of Lemma <a href=\"#hp:opening\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"hp:opening\">12</a>. It is a genuine homeomorphism on target neighborhoods away from their values and accumulation seams. For $p\\geq3$ it satisfies volume Lusin $N$.*\n\n\n2.  *$O$ is a locally finite union of exact affine or PL core images. Every compact subset of such a core has a neighborhood on which $F_b$ and its inverse are exactly those of its affine or PL chart. In particular no point of $O$ has a nontrivial fibre, and $$\\label{hp:residual-volume}\n     \\mathcal L^3(Q\\setminus O)<a_Q\\qquad(Q\\in\\mathcal Q).$$ The compact endpoint rectangles retain their fixed buffers in $O_1$.*\n\n3.  *$F_b=F_\\kappa$ on a neighborhood of $K$. It meets the prescribed fine value tolerance relative to $f$. The choices of $\\kappa$ and of the retained central margins ensure that $F_\\kappa(K)$ stays in the protected central plate neighborhoods.*\n\n\n4.  *When $2<p<3$, there is a locally finite family of marked source cubes $U$ with disjoint closures, away from $K$, such that $$\\label{hp:small-marked-mass}\n     \\int_{\\bigcup U}(1+|Df|^p)<\\varepsilon.$$ For $p\\geq3$ this family is empty.         "anchor": "stmt-hp-full-rank-correction",
        "exact_quote": "Let $p>2$ and let $f:\\Omega\\to\\Lambda$ be an orientation-preserving Sobolev homeomorphism between bounded domains. Let $R$ be the set of its regular differentiation points at which $Df$ has rank three. Let $P\\Subset\\Omega$ be any previously protected compact set disjoint from $R$. Given $\\varepsilon>0$, one can choose finitely many pairwise disjoint buffered source cubes, disjoint from $P$, with centers $x_j\\in R$, radii $r_j$, and positive affine jets $$A_j=Df(x_j),\\qquad\n b_j(x)=f(x_j)+A_j(x-x_j),$$ such that the inner cubes $K_j=x_j+r_jB$ satisfy $$\\label{hp:full-rank-core-tests}\n \\int_{R\\setminus\\bigcup_jK_j}|Df|^p<\\varepsilon,\n \\qquad\n \\sum_j\\int_{K_j}|Df-A_j|^p<\\varepsilon.$$ Their buffered cutoff bands $$E_j=\\{x_j+r_j\\xi:|t(\\xi)|\\leq Cs\\}$$ can have arbitrarily small total $f$-energy, even after multiplication by all the finitely bounded affine factors $C_p|A_j|^p|A_j^{-1}|^p$. On those bands the normalized $f$ is within $cs/4$ of the identity.*\n\n*Write $Q_j=x_j+r_jB_{(C+1)s}$ for the buffered outer cubes. After these choices there are numbers $v_j>0$ and $\\beta>0$ such that every smooth diffeomorphism $k:\\Omega\\to\\Lambda$ satisfying $$\\sup_{Q_j}|k-f|<v_j\\quad\\text{for each }j,\n \\qquad \\sum_j\\int_{E_j}|Dk|^p<\\beta$$ can be changed only inside the associated outer cubes $x_j+r_jB_{2s}$ to a locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism $\\widetilde k:\\Omega\\to\\Lambda$ with $$\\widetilde k=b_j\\quad\\text{on }K_j.$$ The sum of the derivative-error integrals on the inner cubes and their modified shells is less than $\\varepsilon$, after starting the selection with smaller error prescriptions if necessary. The cubes and tests may also be chosen to retain any prescribed positive continuous value tolerance for the final modification.*\n\n*A locally bi-Lipschitz preliminary map in $W^{1,p}(\\Omega;\\mathbb R^3)$ can be used in place of $k$ by first applying Theorem <a href=\"#sm:smoothing\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sm:smoothing\">70</a>, preserving the finite value and band-energy tests with room to spare.",

      },

        "exact_quote": "Suppose $2<p<3$, and let $U$ and $w_U$ be the marked cubes and collars of Proposition <a href=\"#hp:carrier\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"hp:carrier\">15</a>.         "exact_quote": "Let $b_1$ be the protected-well perturbation of Lemma <a href=\"#hp:wells\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"hp:wells\">9</a>.         "exact_quote": "Fix $0<c<m$ with $c<1$. One can choose a locally finite family of interior sites in $\\Lambda$, with one contact at each ordinary site and the two protected contacts at each paired site. The family can include the rectangular paired arrays constructed in Lemma <a href=\"#qt:calibration\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"qt:calibration\">23</a>. Index these site and contact pairs by $i$, writing them as $(q_i,x_i)$, and define $$\\label{qt:obstacle}\n G(q)=\\sup_i\\{F(q_i)+x_i\\cdot(q-q_i)+\\tfrac c2|q-q_i|^2\\},\n \\qquad T=(\\partial G)^{-1},$$ where the supremum also includes the support based at every $q_i\\notin\\Lambda$. Here $q$ is an output of $T$, and $y\\in\\partial G(q)$ is an input. Then $T:\\mathbb R^3\\to\\mathbb R^3$ is single-valued and $c^{-1}$-Lipschitz, equals the identity outside $\\Lambda$, and restricts to a proper onto map of $\\Lambda$ to itself, as finely close to the identity as prescribed.*\n\n\n*Inside $\\Lambda$, $G-c|q|^2/2$ is a locally finite maximum of affine functions. Its diagram has compact convex polyhedral cells. Write $p_i=x_i-cq_i$. Over the relative interior of a face $P$, whose active indices are $I(P)$, its exact input product is $$\\label{qt:product}\n \\partial G(q)=cq+\\mathop{\\mathrm{conv}}\\{p_i:i\\in I(P)\\},\\qquad\n T(cq+v)=q\\quad(q\\in\\mathop{\\mathrm{relint}}P).$$ The two factors have orthogonal direction spaces of complementary dimensions. Every retained support owns a genuine three-dimensional output cell $C_i$. Its closed input block $$\\label{qt:blocks}\n X_i=cC_i+p_i$$ is compactly contained in $O$. These closed blocks are pairwise disjoint and have locally finite, mutually disjoint protective neighborhoods within the exact regions of the carrier. Outside their union the output of $T$ lies in the two-skeleton of the diagram.",

        "exact_quote": "The choices in Proposition <a href=\"#qt:quantizer\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"qt:quantizer\">22</a> can be made together with a locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism $J:\\Lambda\\to\\Lambda$, equal to the identity near every closed $X_i$, such that $TJ$ has an absolute Lipschitz bound. Put $$\\widehat F=JF_b,\\qquad q_0=T\\widehat F.$$ Apart from arbitrarily small prescribed source weight, $q_0$ maps the retained rank-one and rank-two data into the interiors of horizontal rectangular true two-faces. The carrier $\\widehat F$ retains the exact data over the blocks and its relative opening property, and $|Dq_0|\\leq C|DF_b|$ almost everywhere. On the retained compact rank-$k$ data, $k=1,2$, $$\\label{qt:calibrated-gradient}\n Dq_0=a_*^{-1}\\operatorname{proj}_{n^\\perp}DF_\\kappa,\n \\qquad |Dq_0-Df|\\leq C(\\lambda+1-a_*)|Df|,$$ where $c<a_*<1$ may be as close to one as required and $\\lambda$ is the preceding flattening accuracy. The rank is exactly $k$ and $\\ker Df\\subset\\ker Dq_0$. For rank one the rectangle can have any previously prescribed small short-to-long aspect, with its first axis arbitrarily close to the range line of $Dq_0$.     {
      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-qt-subdivision",
        "exact_quote": "The true two-faces of the quantizer diagram have locally finite, conforming subdivisions into convex polygonal subcells $D$ with chosen centers $d_D$. Protected rectangular faces may be kept as rectangles or subdivided by finer rectangular grids. Elsewhere the ratio of diameter to center-boundary clearance has an absolute bound away from arbitrarily small prescribed neighborhoods of the original vertices. Inside those neighborhoods it has a finite bound depending only on the original face. The latter constants can be confined to regions of arbitrarily small weighted $\\int|Dq_0|^p$ cost. Additional rays from a protected center to inserted perimeter vertices can be chosen to avoid almost every retained datum.",

        "exact_quote": "For each subcell $D$, put $$R_{D,e}(t,s)=d_D+r\\bigl(\\xi_e(s)-d_D\\bigr),\\qquad\n r=\\exp(t/L_D),$$ where $\\xi_e$ is arclength on a perimeter subedge and the same arclength label is used in all incident sectors. Choose $L_D$ comparable to the maximum radius of $D$; in a protected rank-one rectangle choose it as the long-axis half-length and choose $d_D$ to be the geometric midpoint of the rectangle. On an open sector, $$\\label{qt:polar-bounds}\n |D_qt|+|D_qs|\\leq C_D/r,\\qquad\n |\\partial_tR_{D,e}|+|\\partial_sR_{D,e}|\\leq C r.$$ The first constant depends only on the clearance ratio, and the second is absolute. For a rectangle of half-length $L$ and half-width $\\gamma L$, and its unit long-axis vector $v_1$, $$\\label{qt:rank-one-polar}\n |D_qt(v_1)|+|D_qs(v_1)|\\leq(1+\\gamma)/r,\n \\qquad\n \\max\\{|\\partial_tR|,|\\partial_sR|\\}\n \\leq\\sqrt{1+\\gamma^2}\\,r.$$",

        "anchor": "stmt-qt-exterior",
        "exact_quote": "Choose a small $r_{u,D}>0$ in every subcell. In input target coordinates remove the full closed blocks $X_i$ and the open cores of the interval prisms over $d_D+r_{u,D}(D-d_D)$, with their ends attached to the full blocks. The closure $M_y$ of the remainder is a locally finite PL three-manifold with boundary. The radial projection in each subcell, identity on subedges, defines a continuous map $$\\pi T:M_y\\longrightarrow\\Gamma,$$ where $\\Gamma$ is the subedge graph. Each component of $M_y$ is a possibly noncompact graph handlebody. In particular every PL embedded compact interior two-sphere bounds a PL ball and $$\\label{qt:exterior-homology}\n H_2(M_y;\\mathbb Z)=0.$$ For intermediate levels there are two standard families of proper walls: $A_D(t)$ is the perimeter at common radial label $t$, times the face-offset interval; $B_e(s)$ is the entire inverse of the intermediate subedge point under $\\pi T$. Walls within one colour are disjoint. Each $A$ is an incompressible annulus and each $B$ is a disk. An incident pair has two boundary intersection points, one on each annular end; a nonincident pair has none. Consequently transverse individually standard walls with this boundary incidence have one spanning intersection arc for each incident pair, and otherwise only circles; every such circle is contractible in both walls.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-qt-central-carrier",
        "exact_quote": "Let $p>2$. Let $T:\\Lambda\\to\\Lambda$ have the properties of Proposition <a href=\"#qt:quantizer\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"qt:quantizer\">22</a>, and let $\\widehat F:\\Omega\\to\\Lambda$ have the carrier properties retained in Lemma <a href=\"#qt:calibration\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"qt:calibration\">23</a>. In particular, $\\widehat F$ is a proper continuous $W^{1,p}_{\\mathrm{loc}}$ carrier with connected fibres and a countable set $E_0$ of nonsingleton values, it has the relative opening property of Lemma <a href=\"#hp:opening\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"hp:opening\">12</a>, and its prescribed maps over neighborhoods of the closed full blocks $X_i$ are PL homeomorphisms. Use the locally finite face subdivision and central prisms of Proposition <a href=\"#qt:exterior\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"qt:exterior\">27</a>. Fix, separately from the central radii, a positive low activation radius $a_D$ in every subcell $D$.*\n\n*The radii $0<r_{u,D}\\ll a_D$ can be chosen so that the resulting closed exterior $M_y$ has the following additional properties. There exist a PL homeomorphism $h_*:\\Omega\\to\\Lambda$, a proper continuous $W^{1,p}_{\\mathrm{loc}}$ map $\\overline K:\\Lambda\\to\\Lambda$, and $$F_*=\\overline K h_*,\\qquad M_x=h_*^{-1}(M_y),\\qquad q_*=TF_* ,$$ such that:*\n\n1.  *$\\overline K$ is the identity on an open neighborhood of the full blocks and of all the removed central prisms. Consequently $F_*^{-1}(M_y)=M_x$, and $F_*=h_*$ on an open neighborhood of $\\partial M_x$. These boundary data are PL and have the originally prescribed values near the full blocks.*\n\n2.  *$\\overline K$, and hence $F_*$, is a fine limit of actual homeomorphisms with these exact data. Its fibres are nonempty and connected, and only countably many of its target values have nonsingleton fibres.*\n\n3.  *All changes from $\\widehat F$ occur in compactly localized, locally finite face neighborhoods whose old and new labels lie in $r<a_D$. The changes meet any prescribed fine value tolerance. Thus $F_*=\\widehat F$ in the complementary high region. On every compact portion of $M_x$ the labels $q_*$, and the radial and perimeter coordinates used there, have finite ambient local Sobolev budgets. No uniform bound for these new low-region budgets is asserted.*\n\n*There is a locally finite closed family $S$ of possible limiting inner cube seams in the changed regions. Away from $S$, the construction has the local fibre formula proved below. The portions of $S$ at which the construction is not already exact lie away from $\\partial M_x$.",

        "exact_quote": "Fix the quantizer, carrier, exterior and boundary data above.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-ms-boundary-collar",
        "exact_quote": "The boundary mesh and the central wall traces can be arranged so that:*\n\n1.  *each central trace in a boundary triangle is a straight normal arc with at most one hit on an individual edge;*\n\n2.  *near each selected sample, a closed label interval has a piecewise-linear ribbon continuation matching the normal-disk prism construction, and distinct intervals of one colour are disjoint;*\n\n3.  *the two-colour pattern throughout the outer collar is jointly locally bi-Lipschitz equivalent to the cut pattern times depth, preserving both parameters;*\n\n4.  *the inverse label slopes and the edge-coarea bounds on the modified collar have fixed local bounds independent of $d_0$, of the excluded belt widths, and of the final mesh and sample scales.*\n\n\n*In normalized square coordinates, if a feature has physical label length $\\ell$, an occupied interval of label length comparable to $c_*w_j$ gives on each crossed boundary edge a fractional width at least $$\\frac{c\\varepsilon c_*w_j}{\\ell H_0}.\n \\label{ms:boundary-width}$$ Here $H_0$ is the local dyadic square scale, $\\varepsilon>0$ is fixed before final sampling, and $c>0$ is independent of the subsequent choices.",

        "anchor": "stmt-wl-relative-pl",
        "exact_quote": "Let $M$ be a three-dimensional PL manifold, possibly with boundary, with a locally finite triangulation. Physical coordinates on $M$ may be obtained from its PL coordinates by locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphisms. Let $(S_j)$ be a locally finite disjoint family of compact, properly embedded, locally flat surfaces. Suppose that each $S_j$ avoids the mesh vertices and has only finitely many, isolated intersections with mesh edges. On a neighborhood of $\\partial M$ suppose the surfaces already have prescribed PL product collars, with transverse edge crossings and straight traces in boundary triangles. The protected collars may be made smaller before the construction.*\n\n*Then the family can be replaced by a family of PL surfaces of the same individual topological types, retaining the prescribed smaller boundary collars, such that the number of intersections of each individual surface with each individual edge does not increase. Every retained interior edge intersection can be required to have a flat transverse disk germ. The changes can be confined to any prescribed neighborhood of the original family and can be arbitrarily small in a prescribed positive continuous position tolerance. No bound on the Lipschitz constants of these preparatory changes is asserted.",

        "anchor": "stmt-wl-normalization",
        "exact_quote": "Let $M$ be an orientable irreducible PL three-manifold with a locally finite triangulation. Let $(S_j)$ be a locally finite family of pairwise disjoint, compact, properly embedded PL surfaces in general position. Each $S_j$ is a disk or an annulus; in the annulus case its core is noncontractible in $M$. Assume that the prescribed boundary traces are straight normal arcs in boundary triangles and that $$\\#(S_j\\cap e)\\leq 1\n       \\quad\\hbox{for every boundary edge $e$ and every $j$}.$$ Then there is a locally finite disjoint family $(S'_j)$ with the same individual topologies, coorientations, and exact boundary traces, consisting of normal triangles and quadrilaterals, such that $$\\#(S'_j\\cap e)\\leq\\#(S_j\\cap e)\n                    \\quad\\hbox{for every $j$ and every edge $e$}.$$ For a finite family the replacements can be obtained by an ambient isotopy relative to the boundary. Consequently any initially prescribed upper bounds on the individual edge counts are retained. This assertion concerns one colour only; it imposes no requirement to preserve the other colour.",

        "anchor": "stmt-ms-normal-templates",
        "exact_quote": "In a normalized tetrahedron fix an endpoint margin $\\gamma>0$. For every normal disk type use its triangle, or the two triangles of a quadrilateral on one chosen combinatorial diagonal. We call these pieces the main triangles and, in the quadrilateral case, call their shared diagonal the main crease. Require all crossing-edge fractions to lie in $[\\gamma,1-\\gamma]$. Compatible within-colour edge orders give disjoint templates. Their separations are at least $c(\\gamma)$ times the minimum edge gap. Between two ordered placements of the same disk type the ordered affine stair prisms give a PL homeomorphism onto the entire shell. If its scalar parameter has range of length at most $w$, then $$|\\nabla u|\\le C(\\gamma)\n       \\max_{e\\text{ crossed}}\\frac{w}{\\Delta_e},\n \\label{ms:normal-slope}$$ where $\\Delta_e$ is the fractional width on the crossed edge.         "anchor": "stmt-wl-pattern",
        "exact_quote": "Let $\\Sigma$ be a compact smooth disk or annulus, let $J$ be a compact interval, and let $E:\\Sigma\\times J\\to C$ be bi-Lipschitz. For finitely many indices $k$, suppose that a Lipschitz function $f_k(z,\\lambda)$ is defined on an open neighborhood of its compact enlarged strip $$K_k=\\{(z,\\lambda):a_k-\\delta_k\\leq f_k(z,\\lambda)\n                         \\leq b_k+\\delta_k\\},\n \\qquad a_k<b_k,\\quad\\delta_k>0.$$ The sets $K_k$ are assumed disjoint, and all relevant strip points belong to these compact sets, with a margin inside their domains of definition. Each strip is the full inverse image of its indicated label interval in its isolated neighborhood: apart from $\\partial\\Sigma$, there is no additional lateral frontier inside the enlarged label interval. At every point of $K_k$ suppose there is a smooth vector field $V$ on a surface neighborhood, tangent to $\\partial\\Sigma$ at boundary points, and a neighborhood in $\\Sigma\\times J$ on which $$D_z f_k(z,\\lambda)V(z)\\geq c>0\n \\quad\\hbox{for almost every }(z,\\lambda).$$ Equivalently one may impose the integrated strict increase along the local $V$-flow for every nearby $\\lambda$. The constant and direction may depend on the neighborhood.*\n\n*Then the simultaneous subdivision of $C$ by the strips $a_k\\leq f_k\\leq b_k$ is jointly bi-Lipschitz trivial over $J$, preserving $f_k$ on each strip and preserving the manifold boundary. For each fixed $\\lambda$, every connected strip is also a bi-Lipschitz product over its $f_k$ parameter. Thus, when its level fibres are the prescribed arcs or circles, it has the full product-box form required in Definition <a href=\"#wl:prestack\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"wl:prestack\">32</a>.",
        "source_id": "PM-368.2"

        "exact_quote": "Consider an equal-weight patch with $W\\leq H$. Its fine triangles therefore have diameter comparable to $W$ and uniformly controlled shapes. The two half-prisms over a fine triangle are triangulated by the fixed ordered stair rule. All their vertex displacements have magnitude at most $A s_\\sigma$, for a fixed $A$.*\n\n3.  *Any subsequent template adjustment in an original tetrahedron is a PL homeomorphism of that tetrahedron with Lipschitz constant and inverse Lipschitz constant at most $L$. It is affine on a partition with a uniformly bounded number of convex polyhedral pieces, whose numbers of faces are uniformly bounded.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-ms-snapping",
        "exact_quote": "Let $\\mathcal G$ be the finite auxiliary triangulation in the patch. Let $\\mathcal C$ and $\\mathcal P$ be disjoint subcomplexes, respectively the canonical and protected subcomplexes. On $\\mathcal C$ suppose that a common subdivision as in Lemma <a href=\"#ms:bounded-complexity\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"ms:bounded-complexity\">59</a> has been fixed, with at most $N$ simplices in each auxiliary simplex. In particular, every master collar domain is a subcomplex of that subdivision and every relevant master parameter $u_j$ is affine there with values in $[0,W]$.*\n\n*On each remaining positive-dimensional auxiliary simplex $D\\notin\\mathcal C$, suppose the old master parameters already have upper local slope at most $B W/h_D$ on their closed parameter parts. Here the upper local slope of a function on a closed set $A$ at $x\\in A$ means $$\\limsup_{\\substack{y\\to x\\\\y\\in A,\\ y\\ne x}}\n \\frac{|u(y)-u(x)|}{|y-x|},$$ with value zero at an isolated point; bounds on different incident cells may be combined by taking their maximum. The master parameters are locally Lipschitz for the fixed configuration.*\n\n*There is a cell-preserving PL homeomorphism $J$ of the patch, from new coordinates to old coordinates, such that:*\n\n1.  *$J$ is the identity on $\\mathcal P$;*\n\n2.  *$\\mathop{\\mathrm{Lip}}(J|_D)\\leq C$ on every auxiliary simplex $D$, with $C$ depending only on $N$, the auxiliary shape bounds, and the dimension;*\n\n3.  *on each positive-dimensional canonical cell $D$, the transported parameter $u_j\\circ J$ has a $C W/h_D$-Lipschitz extension to all of $D$;*\n\n4.  *on every other positive-dimensional cell, the transported parameters have upper local slope at most $C B W/h_D$ on their parameter parts.*\n\n*Consequently the transported upper slope density is at most $C(1+B)W/s_\\sigma=C(1+B)M_\\sigma$, with incident maxima at interfaces. The constants do not depend on the smallest altitude of an old subdivision simplex or on the smallest angle between opposite master sheets. If the outer boundary of the patch belongs to $\\mathcal P$, then $J$ extends by the identity outside the patch. The inverse of $J$ is locally Lipschitz for the fixed configuration, without a uniform bound being required.",

      },

In particular, every master collar domain is a subcomplex of that subdivision and every relevant master parameter $u_j$ is affine there with values in $[0,W]$.*\n\n*On each remaining positive-dimensional auxiliary simplex $D\\notin\\mathcal C$, suppose the old master parameters already have upper local slope at most $B W/h_D$ on their closed parameter parts. Here the upper local slope of a function on a closed set $A$ at $x\\in A$ means $$\\limsup_{\\substack{y\\to x\\\\y\\in A,\\ y\\ne x}}\n \\frac{|u(y)-u(x)|}{|y-x|},$$ with value zero at an isolated point; bounds on different incident cells may be combined by taking their maximum. The constants do not depend on the smallest altitude of an old subdivision simplex or on the smallest angle between opposite master sheets. If the outer boundary of the patch belongs to $\\mathcal P$, then $J$ extends by the identity outside the patch.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-ms-sharp-contract",
        "exact_quote": "Fix $\\eta$, the compact chart and basis bounds, and the finite template choices above. The calibrated islands admit pre-stacks with all the qualitative properties of Definition <a href=\"#wl:prestack\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"wl:prestack\">32</a> and with the following quantitative properties.*\n\n1.  *Throughout an enlarged equal-weight island the pre-slope density is at most $CM_\\sigma$ in aligned units. This constant is independent of microscopic master widths, central crossing angles, final guard gaps, $H$, $W$, and the final level-count tolerance $\\delta'$.*\n\n2.  *In deep regular low-leakage portions, the scalar gradients obey <a href=\"#ms:sharp-scalar\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"ms:sharp-scalar\">[ms:sharp-scalar]</a>. At concurrent independent strips the two-coordinate squared Frobenius cost is at most $2+C\\eta$. At an occupied diagonal transition after routing, the active coordinate has gradient $\\pm\\nabla u_j\\pm\\nabla u_k$, whose squared norm has the same bound. In parallel mode the opponent bands are disjoint in these portions and the squared norm is at most $1+C\\eta$. Occupied-stair speeds multiply these bounds by at most $(1+C\\zeta)^2$.*\n\n\n3.  *In a regular tetrahedron the excluded $CNW$ neighborhoods of its faces, all its main slab creases, and its non-slab disks occupy relative volume at most $$C_N\\left(\\frac WH+\\delta'\\right).\n     \\label{ms:dirty-volume}$$ The canonical protection and broadening margins only change the fixed factor $C_N$. Nonregular tetrahedra, high-leakage tetrahedra, their required fixed-neighbor layers, and patch boundary margins are charged by their full $M^p$-cost.*\n\n*The norm statements concern the smooth compatible label sectors after the combined label barrier, away from central radial activation cutoffs. They are geometric scalar-pair estimates; their physical conversion and the saturation argument are made in Lemma <a href=\"#ha:saturation\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"ha:saturation\">69</a>.",

    {
      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-ms-prestacks",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose the central starting systems have the boundary data of Lemma <a href=\"#ms:boundary-collar\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"ms:boundary-collar\">45</a> and the wall-by-wall edge upper counts used in the separate-colour normalization of Proposition <a href=\"#wl:normalization\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"wl:normalization\">49</a>. Suppose also that the weighted edge tests have been selected as in Lemma <a href=\"#ms:edge-tests\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"ms:edge-tests\">46</a>. The constructions of Sections <a href=\"#sec:mesh\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sec:mesh\">5</a> and <a href=\"#sec:calibrated-islands\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sec:calibrated-islands\">6</a> give the pre-stacks required in Definition <a href=\"#wl:prestack\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"wl:prestack\">32</a>: same-colour compact disjoint collars; opposite arc or circle products with the full parameter rectangles; individual pattern trivializations preserving the opposite parameter; the exact boundary correspondence; and locally bi-Lipschitz changed coordinates in which the relevant endpoint arrangements and parameters are PL.*\n\n*Their pre-parameter slopes admit a density $G$ satisfying the ordinary bound <a href=\"#ms:weak-G\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"ms:weak-G\">[ms:weak-G]</a>, the fixed boundary and chart bounds of Lemma <a href=\"#ms:boundary-collar\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"ms:boundary-collar\">45</a>, and the island bound $G\\le CM_\\sigma$ of Proposition <a href=\"#ms:sharp-contract\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"ms:sharp-contract\">62</a>. All constants in these inequalities may be fixed before choosing final guard gaps, mesh resolutions, and sample weights. Consequently any crude compact-local integral capacities deduced from these inequalities and the conditional edge-variation bounds are independent of those later choices. The actual simultaneous choice of the capacities, meshes, and samples is supplied by Lemma <a href=\"#ha:capacities\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"ha:capacities\">66</a> and Proposition <a href=\"#ha:initial-walls\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"ha:initial-walls\">67</a>.",

    {
      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-ha-sharp-counts",
        "exact_quote": "The meshes and the subsequent stratified samples can be chosen so that the sharp-template count conditions hold outside tetrahedra of arbitrarily small aggregate pre-derivative $p$-cost. More precisely, for the two family counts on an edge $l$, $$\\label{ha:sharp-edge}\n \\frac{N_{l,i}W}{H}\n \\le (1+C(\\zeta+c_*))\n          \\left|(BV)_i\\frac{\\Delta y_l}{H}\\right|+e_l,\n \\qquad e_l\\ge0,$$ and the aggregate $\\sum_lH^3e_l^p$ can be arbitrarily small after all fixed template, transition and physical conversion factors. Given a continuous function $\\eta:M\\to(0,\\infty)$, there is a PL homeomorphism $f_1:M\\to N$ which agrees with $f$ on a neighborhood of $K$ and satisfies $$d_N(f_1(x),f(x))<\\eta(x)\\qquad(x\\in M).$$ Noncompact manifolds are allowed.         "anchor": "stmt-sm-local-extension",
        "exact_quote": "Fix a closed Euclidean cube $B\\subset\\mathbb R^3$, compact sets $C,D\\subset B$ with $C\\subset\\operatorname{int}B$, and an open neighborhood $O$ of $C\\cup D\\cup\\partial B$. If $e:O\\to\\mathbb R^3$ is an embedding, $$\\sup_{x\\in O}|e(x)-x|<\\delta,\n \\qquad e=\\operatorname{id}\\ \\hbox{on }D\\cup\\partial B,$$ then there is a homeomorphism $A:\\mathbb R^3\\to\\mathbb R^3$ such that $$\\label{sm:extension-conclusion}\n A=e\\ \\hbox{on }C,\\qquad\n A=\\operatorname{id}\\ \\hbox{on }D\\cup(\\mathbb R^3\\setminus\\operatorname{int}B),\n \\qquad \\sup_{\\mathbb R^3}|A-\\operatorname{id}|<\\lambda.$$ The number $\\delta$ is uniform over a finite list of fixed normalized configurations $(B,C,D,O)$. <a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Domains and Sobolev homeomorphisms** ([source](#sec:introduction)): Let $\Omega,\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^3$ be domains, meaning nonempty connected open sets. A homeomorphism $f:\Omega\to\Lambda$ belongs to $W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ when its components and their weak first derivatives are in $L^p$.
- **Strong Sobolev approximation** ([source](#sec:introduction)): Strong $W^{1,p}$ approximation requires convergence of both the maps and these derivatives in $L^p$.
- **Fixed-target approximation problem** ([source](#sec:introduction)): The *fixed-target Ball–Evans approximation problem* asks whether one can choose the approximants to be smooth diffeomorphisms from $\Omega$ onto exactly $\Lambda$.
- **Matrix norms** ([source](#pm-h-5)): The symbol $\|A\|$ denotes the Frobenius norm of a matrix, and $\\|A\\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ its operator norm.
- **Fine value tolerance** ([source](#pm-h-5)): A *fine value tolerance* on a domain $U$ is a positive continuous function on $U$.
- **Local bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism** ([source](#pm-h-5)): A locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism has finite Lipschitz constants in both directions on sufficiently small neighborhoods; no global bound is implicit.
- **Volume Lusin property** ([source](#pm-h-7)): A map has the volume Lusin property $N$ if it maps sets of three-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero to sets of measure zero.
- **Deficient-rank data and assignment measures** ([source](#pm-h-8)): Let $R_f$ be the regular set from Lemma <a href="#hp:regularity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="hp:regularity">3</a>, and set $$D=\{x\in R_f:1\le\mathop{\mathrm{rank}}Df(x)\le2\}, \qquad \mu(E)=\int_{E\cap D}(1+\|Df\|^p)\,dx, \qquad \nu=f_\#(\mathbf1_\Omega\,\mathcal L^3).$$
- **Decomposability bundle** ([source](#pm-h-8)): The decomposability bundle $V(\nu,y)$ records the tangent directions of rectifiable curves whose averaged measures are absolutely continuous with respect to $\nu$.
- **Null family of fibres** ([source](#pm-h-11)): A null family below means that only finitely many members meeting a fixed compact localization have diameter greater than any prescribed positive number.
- **Pre-stack contract** ([source](#stmt-wl-prestack)): Let $M_x,M_y$ be the source and target exteriors and let $h_*:M_x\to M_y$ be the fixed reference homeomorphism. A pre-stack system consists of a locally finite, countable, two-colour family of compact collars $$\mathcal E_j:\Sigma_j\times[0,w_j]\longrightarrow C_j\subset M_x, \qquad u_j(\mathcal E_j(z,\lambda))=\lambda,\qquad w_j>0,$$ whose central sampled wall is the level $u_j=w_j/2$, subject to the following conditions. 1. Each $\mathcal E_j$ is a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism onto its image. For colour $A$, $\Sigma_j$ is an annulus whose core is essential in $M_x$; for colour $B$, $\Sigma_j$ is a disk. Each level is properly embedded, and $C_j\cap\partial M_x=\mathcal E_j(\partial\Sigma_j\times[0,w_j])$. The collars of a single colour are disjoint, including their boundaries. The family of closed collars is locally finite. 2. There is a specified affine increasing correspondence from $[0,w_j]$ to a true target label interval $I_j$. On $\partial M_x$ every level has exactly the boundary trace of its specified standard target wall, pulled back by $h_*$. The increasing-$u_j$ coorientation agrees with that target label coorientation at every boundary component; for an annulus this includes both ends. The target incidence says that an incident opposite-colour pair has two boundary intersection points, one on each annulus end, and that a nonincident pair has none. 3. For each opposite-colour pair $j,k$, the intersection $C_j\cap C_k$ is a finite disjoint union of bi-Lipschitz product boxes $$Q\times[0,w_j]\times[0,w_k], \qquad u_j=\lambda,\quad u_k=\mu,$$ where $Q$ is a circle or a compact interval. The interval endpoints are exactly the parts of that box on $\partial M_x$. These are full parameter rectangles: no box terminates at an interior value of either parameter. The level sheets meet transversely in these product coordinates. There are no further intersection pieces. In particular, for an incident pair every level pair has the specified single spanning arc, together with possible circles; a nonincident pair has only possible circles. 4. In each collar the subdivision by all its opposite-colour boxes is jointly bi-Lipschitz trivial over $u_j$, preserving every concurrent opposite parameter. Precisely, for some reference level there is a bi-Lipschitz product parametrization that carries every intersection box, every complementary piece, and every boundary piece at the reference level to its counterpart at each level; on an opposite box it preserves $u_k$. Its restriction to a boundary piece remains in $\partial M_x$. No uniform quantitative bound for this trivialization is required. 5. The ambient PL structure and the physical metric are compatible in the following explicit sense. Every locally finite arrangement of pieces obtained by finitely many constant or affine parameter cuts on each compact set admits common ambient coordinate changes that are locally bi-Lipschitz in the physical metric and make the pieces PL simultaneously. These changes preserve the manifold boundary and the specified incidences. Separate unrelated PL charts for individual pieces do not suffice for this requirement. 6. Every $u_j$ is Lipschitz on its closed collar in the physical metric. Any subsequent estimate using a density $G$ assumes, as an additional quantitative input, a nonnegative locally measurable $G$ dominating the point-to-base upper local slopes $$\operatorname{lip}_{C_j}u_j(x) =\limsup_{\substack{y\to x\\y\in C_j,\ y\ne x}} \frac{\|u_j(y)-u_j(x)\|}{\|y-x\|}.$$ Use the adjacent maxima at internal interfaces and include both parameter bounds at an essential intersection box. On exceptional collar-boundary or mesh-interface strata one may enlarge $G$ to the actual local Lipschitz bounds of the fixed compact collars. These strata, in the common working coordinates or their bi-Lipschitz images, have zero volume; the enlargement therefore changes no volume capacity. This convention does not require a two-point Lipschitz bound across gaps of a nonconvex union of pieces. The contract alone asserts neither an integral estimate for $G$ nor independence of that estimate from later choices of guards.
- **Guards and prior capacities** ([source](#stmt-wl-guards)): Choose a locally finite compact cover of $M_x$ by smaller buffered coordinate regions $K_a$, with larger regions $U_a$ carrying fixed bi-Lipschitz ball or half-ball charts. All smaller regions have positive margins in the larger charts. Fix finite numbers $C_a$ as upper capacities for $$\label{wl:prior-capacity} \int_{U_a}G^p\leq C_a.$$ These numbers, the coordinate bounds and the prescribed continuous label accuracies are fixed before guards, sample weights and the final resolution are chosen. A guard system is obtained from a sufficiently fine homeomorphic approximation $h_g$ to $F_*$, agreeing with $h_*$ on the exact boundary data and respecting the exteriors. Choose a locally finite source net of sufficiently small local spacing. For every net point $g$, choose two paths in the constant $Th_g$ fibre from $g$ to boundary anchors whose $h_*$-images are extremal points of the target fibre on distinct full blocks, and let $\kappa_g$ be their union. Thus $\kappa_g$ is compact and connected, and each of its points has a path within $\kappa_g$ to a boundary anchor. Write $q_g=Th_g(g)$ and require $Th_g$ to be sufficiently close to $q_*$. The pre-stacks must be disjoint from all $\kappa_g$.
- **Integral capacity** ([source](#ha:guard-schedule)): Here a capacity means a finite upper bound for a local integral $\int G^p$, not a Sobolev capacity of a set.
- **Point-to-base upper local slope** ([source](#stmt-ms-snapping)): Here the upper local slope of a function on a closed set $A$ at $x\in A$ means $$\limsup_{\substack{y\to x\\y\in A,\ y\ne x}} \frac{\|u(y)-u(x)\|}{\|y-x\|},$$ with value zero at an isolated point; bounds on different incident cells may be combined by taking their maximum.

Each $\\mathcal E_j$ is a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism onto its image. For colour $A$, $\\Sigma_j$ is an annulus whose core is essential in $M_x$; for colour $B$, $\\Sigma_j$ is a disk. On $\\partial M_x$ every level has exactly the boundary trace of its specified standard target wall, pulled back by $h_*$. The increasing-$u_j$ coorientation agrees with that target label coorientation at every boundary component; for an annulus this includes both ends. The interval endpoints are exactly the parts of that box on $\\partial M_x$. These are full parameter rectangles: no box terminates at an interior value of either parameter. The level sheets meet transversely in these product coordinates. There are no further intersection pieces. In particular, for an incident pair every level pair has the specified single spanning arc, together with possible circles; a nonincident pair has only possible circles.\n\n4. Every locally finite arrangement of pieces obtained by finitely many constant or affine parameter cuts on each compact set admits common ambient coordinate changes that are locally bi-Lipschitz in the physical metric and make the pieces PL simultaneously. On exceptional collar-boundary or mesh-interface strata one may enlarge $G$ to the actual local Lipschitz bounds of the fixed compact collars. These strata, in the common working coordinates or their bi-Lipschitz images, have zero volume; the enlargement therefore changes no volume capacity. This convention does not require a two-point Lipschitz bound across gaps of a nonconvex union of pieces. The contract alone asserts neither an integral estimate for $G$ nor independence of that estimate from later choices of guards.",

| q-local-tolerance-upper-bound | Positive Lipschitz tolerance minorant | ≤ | $\min\{a(x),1,L\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(x,\mathbb R^n\setminus U)\}$ | The positive Lipschitz constant and continuous upper tolerance are prescribed. |
| q-flattening-retained-gradient-error | Flattened derivative discrepancy on retained data | ≤ | $C\lambda\|Df\|$ | The flattening parameter varies in the stated interval; the constant is absolute. |
| q-cubical-shell-energy | Cubical cutoff shell energy | ≤ | $C_p\int_{\|t\|\leq Cs}\|Dh\|^p$ | The dyadic shell parameter is sufficiently small and the input satisfies the prescribed boundary closeness. |
| q-regular-affine-core-energy | Energy of regular affine implantation | ≤ | $C_p\int_{V_b}\|DF\|^p$ | The constant is independent of the affine jet condition number; test accuracy may depend on fixed jet bounds. |
| q-carrier-residual-target-volume | Residual target volume in a Whitney cube | < | $a_Q$ | Residual thresholds are prescribed after endpoint cores and buffers are fixed. |
| q-marked-interior-compression | Total compressed marked-interior derivative energy | ≤ | $C_p b+\varepsilon_0$ | The preliminary locally bi-Lipschitz map is fixed before its interior compression parameters. |
| q-product-quantizer-lipschitz-bound | Quantizer Lipschitz constant | ≤ | $c^{-1}$ | The strongly convex obstacle and prescribed locally finite sites satisfy the proposition. |
| q-calibrated-deficient-gradient-error | Calibrated retained gradient discrepancy | ≤ | $C(\lambda+1-a_*)\|Df\|$ | The flattening accuracy and active scalar fraction can approach their stated limiting values. |
| q-retained-root-parameter-length | Occupied root-parameter length | ≥ | $(1-\zeta)w_j$ | The positive length-loss tolerance is prescribed per root. |
| q-spherical-connector-cost | Cost of a spherical connecting path | ≤ | $C_p R^{1-2/p}\left(\int_{\Sigma_R}g^p\,d\mathcal H^2\right)^{1/p}.$ | The exponent exceeds the spherical threshold; fixed bi-Lipschitz changes alter only the constant. |
| q-neighbor-majorant-power-control | Weighted power sum of the neighboring majorant | ≤ | $C_{p,D,\theta}\sum_\sigma H^3m_\sigma^p$ | The kernel decay is fixed below the stated reciprocal-degree threshold. |
| q-broadened-strip-halfwidth | Constant broadened strip half-width | = | $(1-C\eta)W/2$ | The slot slack leaves strict separation below half the slab gap. |
| q-sharp-scalar-gradient | Broadened scalar gradient norm | ≤ | $1+C\eta$ | Remaining tolerances are smaller than the prescribed slot-loss scale. |
| q-physical-saturation-gradient-error | Derivative approximation error on saturation interiors | ≤ | $C_p(\eta+\gamma)(1+E)+\text{freely small errors}$ | The leading constant is independent of compact jet and chart bounds; later errors are chosen after their multipliers. |
| q-smoothing-strong-error | Strong smoothing error | < | $\varepsilon$ | Any finite smoothing exponent in the stated range and any positive continuous value tolerance. |

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-local-minorants** [claim](#stmt-pre-local-tolerances) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pre-local-tolerances): Infimal Lipschitz minorant and locally finite smooth partition of unity. -> Compatible positive local bounds and summable errors.
- **step-regularity** [claim](#stmt-hp-regularity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hp-regularity): Spherical Sobolev embedding, openness, Lipschitz decomposition and area formula. -> Ordinary regular jets, deficient image nullity and the stated Lusin regime.
- **step-transverse-graph-null-data** [claim](#stmt-hp-cone-null) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hp-cone-null): Transport curve tangents into the bundle, apply the converse differentiability theorem, then compact-convex minimax. -> A common full-measure graph-null set in each selected transverse direction.
- **step-thin-bands-and-flattening** [claim](#stmt-hp-flattening) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hp-flattening): Cone-order antichains, compact graph-family near-hit estimates and triangular vertical collapse. -> Separated plate data with preserved ranks and strict flattening approximations.
- **step-protected-wells** [claim](#stmt-hp-wells) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hp-wells): Smooth paired wells, global support gaps and target-volume averaging of endpoint assignments. -> Protected paired contacts with compact regular or exceptional inverse assignments.
- **step-skeleton-and-cutoff** [claim](#stmt-hp-cutoff) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hp-cutoff): Finite normalized skeleton immersions, inverse-branch lifting, weighted overlap summation and collapsed hole fillings. -> Image-preserving exact cubical core with universal shell energy control.
- **step-relative-opening** [claim](#stmt-hp-opening) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hp-opening): Disjoint target neighborhoods, upper semicontinuity of proper fibres and tame ball extensions. -> Fine homeomorphic opening retaining exact prescribed regions.
- **step-exceptional-and-regular-implants** [claim](#stmt-hp-regular-implant) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hp-regular-implant): Phase-averaged exceptional cubes and regular target-normalized affine cutoff estimates. -> Exact cores with exceptional costs isolated and universal regular charging.
- **step-carrier-rounds** [claim](#stmt-hp-carrier) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hp-carrier): Fix endpoint exact regions first, then prescribe residual target thresholds and fill remaining assignments. -> Proper exact carrier with buffered regional and marked-collar budgets.
- **step-smooth-cutoff-and-reservation** [claim](#stmt-hp-full-rank-correction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hp-full-rank-correction): Finite smooth filling models, strict squeezes and Vitali selection with jet factors fixed before shell errors. -> Reserved affine cubes and tests sufficient for postponed correction.
- **step-poisson-and-contact-curvature** [claim](#stmt-qt-contact) / [proof](#proof-stmt-qt-contact): Localized periodic Poisson perturbations, protected support gaps, convex-envelope semiconcavity and conjugacy. -> Interior contacts in exact regions and a quadratic dual gap.
- **step-product-quantizer** [claim](#stmt-qt-quantizer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-qt-quantizer): Locally finite support localization and inversion of a strongly monotone subdifferential. -> Proper target quantizer with orthogonal products and protected full input blocks.
- **step-calibration-and-strict-quantizer** [claim](#stmt-qt-calibration) / [proof](#proof-stmt-qt-calibration): Paired Cartesian arrays, scalar redistribution, contraction for the inverse and phase averaging. -> Calibrated rectangular face labels and strict target approximations.
- **step-face-polar-exterior** [claim](#stmt-qt-exterior) / [proof](#proof-stmt-qt-exterior): Conforming convex subdivision, logarithmic polar coordinates and explicit graph-handlebody decomposition. -> Irreducible exteriors with standard annular and disk walls.
- **step-central-carrier-and-edge-opening** [claim](#stmt-qt-edge-matching) / [proof](#proof-stmt-qt-edge-matching): Low-radius skeletal modification, proper homeomorphic limits and local fibre identification transferred to old relative tests. -> Exact exterior boundary data and a common opening preserving edge hits.
- **step-feature-stairs** [claim](#stmt-wl-stairs) / [proof](#proof-stmt-wl-stairs): Ordered slots, occupied-length allocation, bounded-test variance and integrable-tail truncation. -> Fine stairs with controlled root speed and weighted sampling density.
- **step-routing-and-periods** [claim](#stmt-wl-period) / [proof](#proof-stmt-wl-period): Diagonal partial isometries, unique backwards ancestry, whole-collar visit control and compact cycle capping. -> Proper routed layers with conserved oriented periods.
- **step-guard-barrier** [claim](#stmt-wl-barrier) / [proof](#proof-stmt-wl-barrier): Graph potentials, weighted periods, path coarea, spherical averaging and disjoint-ball packing. -> Layer-support confinement with guard spacing chosen from prior data.
- **step-stability-and-conditional-realization** [claim](#stmt-wl-realization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-wl-realization): Finite stable routing trees, gate-ball decompositions, parameter-preserving products and bi-Lipschitz coning. -> Conditional homeomorphic realization and pinned point labels.
- **step-parameter-cost-and-strict-compositions** [claim](#stmt-wl-strict) / [proof](#proof-stmt-wl-strict): Occupied stairs isolate scalar derivatives; strict factors converge through compatible tangential strata. -> Locally bi-Lipschitz target compositions with arbitrarily small local Sobolev error.
- **step-working-meshes-and-boundary** [claim](#stmt-ms-boundary-collar) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ms-boundary-collar): Compatible meshes and lattice insertions, contraction-based boundary warp, generic vertices, straight chords and joint ribbons. -> Prepared boundary traces and local inverse-label bounds independent of final collar thickness.
- **step-generic-edge-tests** [claim](#stmt-ms-edge-tests) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ms-edge-tests): Ambient vertex densities, Sobolev slicing and conditional stratified coarea sampling. -> ACL edges, finite generic hits and conditional count charges.
- **step-relative-wall-normalization** [claim](#stmt-wl-normalization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-wl-normalization): Relative PL preparation, flat crossing germs, face-circle removal, compression and bigon moves. -> Separate-colour normal disks retaining every individual edge upper count.
- **step-weak-simultaneous-collars** [claim](#stmt-ms-weak-templates) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ms-weak-templates): Normal stair prisms, finite robust transverse templates and intrinsic monotone-flow pattern tests. -> Weak pre-stacks with simultaneous product structure and count-controlled slopes.
