Use there a target tolerance $a_\\Lambda$ satisfying $$a_\\Lambda(y)\\leq\\tfrac14 a(f^{-1}(y)),$$ and then fix the resulting rank data and endpoint protections of Lemma <a href=\"#hp:wells\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"hp:wells\">9</a>. Fix also an enlargement factor $A>1$ for the marked collars, before assigning their facet budgets, and let $\\varepsilon>0$. After a total $\\mu$-loss smaller than $\\varepsilon$, a first round of choices gives $\\kappa>0$, a compact retained source set $K$, a continuous proper onto carrier $F_b^1:\\Omega\\to\\Lambda$, an exact open target set $O_1$, and compact endpoint rectangles strictly inside $O_1$. These choices precede any prescribed residual-volume thresholds. Fix a locally finite target Whitney tiling $\\mathcal Q$, and choose arbitrary numbers $a_Q>0$ for $Q\\in\\mathcal Q$, after $O_1$ and the endpoint buffers have been determined. A second round gives $F_b:\\Omega\\to\\Lambda$ and $O\\supset O_1$ such that:*\n\n1.  *$F_b$ is continuous, proper and onto, belongs to $W^{1,p}_{\\rm loc}$, and has only the countable tame ball fibres of Lemma <a href=\"#hp:opening\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"hp:opening\">12</a>. It is a genuine homeomorphism on target neighborhoods away from their values and accumulation seams. For $p\\geq3$ it satisfies volume Lusin $N$.*\n\n\n2.  *$O$ is a locally finite union of exact affine or PL core images. Every compact subset of such a core has a neighborhood on which $F_b$ and its inverse are exactly those of its affine or PL chart. In particular no point of $O$ has a nontrivial fibre, and $$\\label{hp:residual-volume}\n     \\mathcal L^3(Q\\setminus O)<a_Q\\qquad(Q\\in\\mathcal Q).$$ The compact endpoint rectangles retain their fixed buffers in $O_1$.*\n\n3.  *$F_b=F_\\kappa$ on a neighborhood of $K$. It meets the prescribed fine value tolerance relative to $f$. The choices of $\\kappa$ and of the retained central margins ensure that $F_\\kappa(K)$ stays in the protected central plate neighborhoods.*\n\n\n4.  *When $2<p<3$, there is a locally finite family of marked source cubes $U$ with disjoint closures, away from $K$, such that $$\\label{hp:small-marked-mass}\n     \\int_{\\bigcup U}(1+|Df|^p)<\\varepsilon.$$ For $p\\geq3$ this family is empty. Off the marked cubes the energy has the universal buffered regional estimate described below.*\n\n\n5.  *Write $C_U(w)$ for a cube-radius collar of physical width $w$ about $\\partial U$. For the prescribed enlargement factor $A$, the widths $w_U>0$ can be chosen after both rounds, with disjoint enlarged marked cubes, so that $$\\label{hp:marked-collar-budget}\n     \\sum_U\\frac{\\ell_U}{w_U}\n                 \\int_{C_U(Aw_U)}|DF_b|^p<\\varepsilon.$$ The same bound, multiplied by the $p$th power of the Lipschitz constant, holds after a uniformly Lipschitz output composition. The enlarged cubes may still have original $(1+|Df|^p)$-mass less than $2\\varepsilon$.*\n\n\n*The regional estimate in <span class=\"upright\">(iv)</span> has the following meaning. Suppose a locally finite family of regional tests $A_j$ and two successive small open buffered enlargements $A_j^{[1]}$ and $A_j^{[2]}$ are prescribed before the implants are made. All implants may be chosen so fine that $$\\label{hp:regional-energy}\n \\int_{A_j\\setminus\\bigcup U}|DF_b|^p\n       \\leq C_p\\int_{A_j^{[2]}}|Df|^p\n       \\qquad\\hbox{for every }j.$$ Here each enlargement has positive local buffer, the supports and comparison boxes meeting $A_j$ fit inside its first enlargement at the corresponding round, and $C_p$ is independent of all selected jet condition numbers, residual thresholds, and PL reference-map constants. In particular the tests may be reserved full-rank cut shells or ordinary regions outside prescribed interiors. The same construction works for summably weighted such tests toward the ends of the open domains.",
          "source_id": "PM-368.2"
        }
      ],

          "anchor": "stmt-hp-full-rank-correction",
          "exact_quote": "Let $p>2$ and let $f:\\Omega\\to\\Lambda$ be an orientation-preserving Sobolev homeomorphism between bounded domains. Let $R$ be the set of its regular differentiation points at which $Df$ has rank three. Let $P\\Subset\\Omega$ be any previously protected compact set disjoint from $R$. Given $\\varepsilon>0$, one can choose finitely many pairwise disjoint buffered source cubes, disjoint from $P$, with centers $x_j\\in R$, radii $r_j$, and positive affine jets $$A_j=Df(x_j),\\qquad\n b_j(x)=f(x_j)+A_j(x-x_j),$$ such that the inner cubes $K_j=x_j+r_jB$ satisfy $$\\label{hp:full-rank-core-tests}\n \\int_{R\\setminus\\bigcup_jK_j}|Df|^p<\\varepsilon,\n \\qquad\n \\sum_j\\int_{K_j}|Df-A_j|^p<\\varepsilon.$$ Their buffered cutoff bands $$E_j=\\{x_j+r_j\\xi:|t(\\xi)|\\leq Cs\\}$$ can have arbitrarily small total $f$-energy, even after multiplication by all the finitely bounded affine factors $C_p|A_j|^p|A_j^{-1}|^p$. On those bands the normalized $f$ is within $cs/4$ of the identity.*\n\n*Write $Q_j=x_j+r_jB_{(C+1)s}$ for the buffered outer cubes. After these choices there are numbers $v_j>0$ and $\\beta>0$ such that every smooth diffeomorphism $k:\\Omega\\to\\Lambda$ satisfying $$\\sup_{Q_j}|k-f|<v_j\\quad\\text{for each }j,\n \\qquad \\sum_j\\int_{E_j}|Dk|^p<\\beta$$ can be changed only inside the associated outer cubes $x_j+r_jB_{2s}$ to a locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism $\\widetilde k:\\Omega\\to\\Lambda$ with $$\\widetilde k=b_j\\quad\\text{on }K_j.$$ The sum of the derivative-error integrals on the inner cubes and their modified shells is less than $\\varepsilon$, after starting the selection with smaller error prescriptions if necessary. The cubes and tests may also be chosen to retain any prescribed positive continuous value tolerance for the final modification.*\n\n*A locally bi-Lipschitz preliminary map in $W^{1,p}(\\Omega;\\mathbb R^3)$ can be used in place of $k$ by first applying Theorem <a href=\"#sm:smoothing\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sm:smoothing\">70</a>, preserving the finite value and band-energy tests with room to spare.",
          "source_id": "PM-368.2"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-hp-smooth-cutoff",
          "exact_quote": "Under the hypotheses of Lemma <a href=\"#hp:cutoff\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"hp:cutoff\">11</a>, suppose in addition that $h$ and its inverse are smooth on the neighborhoods in use. For every $\\varepsilon_0>0$ there is instead a locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism $F$ onto the same image, equal to the identity on $B$ and equal to $h$ near and outside $\\partial B_{2s}$, such that $$\\label{hp:smooth-cutoff-energy}\n \\int_{0<t<2s}|DF|^p\n \\leq C_p\\int_{|t|\\leq Cs}|Dh|^p+\\varepsilon_0.$$ The local bi-Lipschitz constants may depend on $h,s$, and $\\varepsilon_0$. In particular no uniform inverse Lipschitz bound is asserted as $\\varepsilon_0\\downarrow0$.",
          "source_id": "PM-368.2"
        }
      ],

      "inputs": [

          "anchor": "stmt-qt-contact",
          "exact_quote": "Let $\\phi$ be the lower convex envelope of $\\psi$ from Lemma <a href=\"#qt:poisson\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"qt:poisson\">20</a>, and let $$F(q)=\\phi^*(q)=\\sup_x\\{q\\cdot x-\\psi(x)\\}.$$ There is an absolute $C_0$ such that $\\phi$ is $C^{1,1}$ and $0\\leq D^2\\phi\\leq C_0 I$ in the distributional sense. With $m=1/C_0$ reduced if necessary, every actual contact maximizer $x_i$ at slope $q_i$ satisfies $$\\label{qt:dual-gap}\n F(q)\\geq F(q_i)+x_i\\cdot(q-q_i)+\\tfrac m2|q-q_i|^2.$$ For any requested fine motion tolerance the perturbations can be chosen so that all contact maximizers at $q$ lie within that tolerance of $q$. For $q\\notin\\Lambda$ the unique maximizer is $q$ and $F(q)=|q|^2/2$. For $q\\in\\Lambda$ every maximizer lies in $O$; over a compact subset of $\\Lambda$ their union is compactly contained in $O$.",
          "source_id": "PM-368.2"

          "anchor": "stmt-qt-poisson",
          "exact_quote": "Let $b_1$ be the protected-well perturbation of Lemma <a href=\"#hp:wells\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"hp:wells\">9</a>. The well sizes can first be chosen sufficiently small, and the residual volume prescriptions for $\\Lambda\\setminus O$ in Proposition <a href=\"#hp:carrier\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"hp:carrier\">15</a> can subsequently be chosen sufficiently small, so that there is $b_2\\in C^\\infty(\\Lambda)$, zero outside $\\Lambda$, with the following properties. For an absolute $C$, $$\\label{qt:laplacian}\n \\psi(x)=\\tfrac12|x|^2+b_1(x)+b_2(x),\\qquad\n \\Delta\\psi\\leq C\\text{ in }\\Lambda,\\qquad\n \\Delta\\psi<0\\text{ in }\\Lambda\\setminus O.$$ The function $b_2$ vanishes on neighborhoods of all protected endpoint boxes, every prescribed affine support indexed by a protected horizontal slope remains a global support of $\\psi$, and, with arbitrarily small $\\epsilon>0$, $$\\label{qt:potential-smallness}\n |b_1+b_2|\\leq\\epsilon\\delta^2,\\qquad\n b_1+b_2=o\\bigl(\\mathop{\\mathrm{dist}}(x,\\mathbb R^3\\setminus\\Lambda)^2\\bigr)\n \\quad(x\\to\\partial\\Lambda).$$",

          "anchor": "stmt-qt-quantizer",
          "exact_quote": "Fix $0<c<m$ with $c<1$. One can choose a locally finite family of interior sites in $\\Lambda$, with one contact at each ordinary site and the two protected contacts at each paired site. The family can include the rectangular paired arrays constructed in Lemma <a href=\"#qt:calibration\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"qt:calibration\">23</a>. Index these site and contact pairs by $i$, writing them as $(q_i,x_i)$, and define $$\\label{qt:obstacle}\n G(q)=\\sup_i\\{F(q_i)+x_i\\cdot(q-q_i)+\\tfrac c2|q-q_i|^2\\},\n \\qquad T=(\\partial G)^{-1},$$ where the supremum also includes the support based at every $q_i\\notin\\Lambda$. Here $q$ is an output of $T$, and $y\\in\\partial G(q)$ is an input. Then $T:\\mathbb R^3\\to\\mathbb R^3$ is single-valued and $c^{-1}$-Lipschitz, equals the identity outside $\\Lambda$, and restricts to a proper onto map of $\\Lambda$ to itself, as finely close to the identity as prescribed.*\n\n\n*Inside $\\Lambda$, $G-c|q|^2/2$ is a locally finite maximum of affine functions. Its diagram has compact convex polyhedral cells. Write $p_i=x_i-cq_i$. Over the relative interior of a face $P$, whose active indices are $I(P)$, its exact input product is $$\\label{qt:product}\n \\partial G(q)=cq+\\mathop{\\mathrm{conv}}\\{p_i:i\\in I(P)\\},\\qquad\n T(cq+v)=q\\quad(q\\in\\mathop{\\mathrm{relint}}P).$$ The two factors have orthogonal direction spaces of complementary dimensions.           "anchor": "stmt-qt-calibration",
          "exact_quote": "The choices in Proposition <a href=\"#qt:quantizer\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"qt:quantizer\">22</a> can be made together with a locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism $J:\\Lambda\\to\\Lambda$, equal to the identity near every closed $X_i$, such that $TJ$ has an absolute Lipschitz bound.           "anchor": "stmt-qt-exterior",
          "exact_quote": "Choose a small $r_{u,D}>0$ in every subcell. In input target coordinates remove the full closed blocks $X_i$ and the open cores of the interval prisms over $d_D+r_{u,D}(D-d_D)$, with their ends attached to the full blocks. The closure $M_y$ of the remainder is a locally finite PL three-manifold with boundary. The radial projection in each subcell, identity on subedges, defines a continuous map $$\\pi T:M_y\\longrightarrow\\Gamma,$$ where $\\Gamma$ is the subedge graph. Each component of $M_y$ is a possibly noncompact graph handlebody. In particular every PL embedded compact interior two-sphere bounds a PL ball and $$\\label{qt:exterior-homology}\n H_2(M_y;\\mathbb Z)=0.$$ For intermediate levels there are two standard families of proper walls: $A_D(t)$ is the perimeter at common radial label $t$, times the face-offset interval; $B_e(s)$ is the entire inverse of the intermediate subedge point under $\\pi T$. Walls within one colour are disjoint. Each $A$ is an incompressible annulus and each $B$ is a disk. An incident pair has two boundary intersection points, one on each annular end; a nonincident pair has none. Consequently transverse individually standard walls with this boundary incidence have one spanning intersection arc for each incident pair, and otherwise only circles; every such circle is contractible in both walls.",
          "source_id": "PM-368.2"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-qt-subdivision",
          "exact_quote": "The true two-faces of the quantizer diagram have locally finite, conforming subdivisions into convex polygonal subcells $D$ with chosen centers $d_D$. Additional rays from a protected center to inserted perimeter vertices can be chosen to avoid almost every retained datum.",
          "source_id": "PM-368.2"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-qt-polar",
          "exact_quote": "For each subcell $D$, put $$R_{D,e}(t,s)=d_D+r\\bigl(\\xi_e(s)-d_D\\bigr),\\qquad\n r=\\exp(t/L_D),$$ where $\\xi_e$ is arclength on a perimeter subedge and the same arclength label is used in all incident sectors. Choose $L_D$ comparable to the maximum radius of $D$; in a protected rank-one rectangle choose it as the long-axis half-length and choose $d_D$ to be the geometric midpoint of the rectangle.           "anchor": "stmt-qt-edge-matching",
          "exact_quote": "Use the carrier and exterior of Lemma <a href=\"#qt:central-carrier\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"qt:central-carrier\">28</a>. Assume:*\n\n1.  *the entire union $W=\\bigcup\\mathcal W$ is relatively closed in $M_y$ and avoids all nonsingleton values of $\\overline K$;*\n\n2.  *the actual hit set $H=(\\bigcup\\mathcal E)\\cap F_*^{-1}(W)$ is finite on compact localizations, and no hit outside the exact regions lies on $S$.*\n\n*Then there are homeomorphisms $f_n:\\Omega\\to\\Lambda$ converging finely to $F_*$, equal to $F_*$ on a neighborhood of $\\partial M_x$ and on the other prescribed exact regions, for which $$f_n^{-1}(W_0)\\cap e=F_*^{-1}(W_0)\\cap e\n \\quad\\text{for every }W_0\\in\\mathcal W, e\\in\\mathcal E.$$ In particular each restriction maps $M_x$ onto $M_y$ with the exact prescribed boundary map. Fix, separately from the central radii, a positive low activation radius $a_D$ in every subcell $D$.*\n\n*The radii $0<r_{u,D}\\ll a_D$ can be chosen so that the resulting closed exterior $M_y$ has the following additional properties.           "anchor": "stmt-wl-stairs",
          "exact_quote": "On a feature interval of length $\\ell$, one can choose $N$ equal weights $w_j=w$ with $Nw/\\ell=1+O(\\zeta)$, and construct an endpoint-fixing nondecreasing stair $S$, constant outside the selected $p_j(E_j)$, such that its total increase over each $I_j$ is $\\ell/N$.       "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-wl-period",
          "exact_quote": "Let $L=L_{j,\\lambda}$ be a good routed surface.           "anchor": "stmt-ms-snapping",
          "exact_quote": "Let $\\mathcal G$ be the finite auxiliary triangulation in the patch. In particular, every master collar domain is a subcomplex of that subdivision and every relevant master parameter $u_j$ is affine there with values in $[0,W]$.*\n\n*On each remaining positive-dimensional auxiliary simplex $D\\notin\\mathcal C$, suppose the old master parameters already have upper local slope at most $B W/h_D$ on their closed parameter parts. Here the upper local slope of a function on a closed set $A$ at $x\\in A$ means $$\\limsup_{\\substack{y\\to x\\\\y\\in A,\\ y\\ne x}}\n \\frac{|u(y)-u(x)|}{|y-x|},$$ with value zero at an isolated point; bounds on different incident cells may be combined by taking their maximum. If the outer boundary of the patch belongs to $\\mathcal P$, then $J$ extends by the identity outside the patch.           "exact_quote": "Consider an equal-weight patch with $W\\leq H$.           "exact_quote": "<span id=\"main:theorem\" label=\"main:theorem\"></span>Let $\\Omega,\\Lambda\\subset\\mathbb R^3$ be bounded domains, let $2<p<\\infty$, and let $f:\\Omega\\to\\Lambda$ be a homeomorphism in $W^{1,p}(\\Omega;\\mathbb R^3)$.           "anchor": "stmt-hp-hide-cubes",
          "exact_quote": "Suppose $2<p<3$, and let $U$ and $w_U$ be the marked cubes and collars of Proposition <a href=\"#hp:carrier\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"hp:carrier\">15</a>.         {
          "anchor": "stmt-sm-pl-smoothing",
          "exact_quote": "The conclusion of Theorem <a href=\"#sm:smoothing\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sm:smoothing\">70</a> holds if $H$ is replaced by a locally finite PL homeomorphism $h:\\Omega\\to\\Omega'$ in $W^{1,p}(\\Omega;\\mathbb R^3)$.",

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-fixed-target-forward-approximation**: Every input satisfying the stated bounded-domain, exponent and homeomorphism hypotheses admits smooth diffeomorphic approximants onto the identical target, with strong convergence of values and forward derivatives.
- **invariant-prior-capacities**: The local integral capacities must be fixed independently of guard spacing and final mesh resolution before selecting guards, meshes and samples.
- **invariant-conditional-wall-realization**: Wall realization preserves the prescribed boundary map and occupied affine label correspondence, conditional on the complete pre-stack contract, guard avoidance, ordered sample intervals and previously fixed integral capacities.
- **invariant-parameter-cost-without-extension-factor**: Exterior derivative costs depend on the prescribed scalar parameter differentials and target speeds, without a derivative factor from the ambient realization or a factor from the number of routing switches.
- **invariant-directed-snapping-control**: The snapping map runs from new coordinates to old coordinates and has uniform forward Lipschitz control. Its inverse has only an input-dependent local bound; protected cells remain fixed.
- **invariant-strong-smoothing-with-fine-values**: A globally Sobolev, locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism admits smooth diffeomorphic approximation with arbitrary positive continuous pointwise value tolerance and exactly the original target.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-inverse-and-singular-energy-convergence**: Treat forward approximation as a guarantee of inverse Sobolev convergence or convergence of elastic energies with singular determinant penalties. -> Smooth inverses and strong forward convergence do not supply either additional convergence conclusion.
- **anti-naive-smoothing-injectivity**: Implement the approximation by ordinary convolution or fine vertex interpolation and assume injectivity survives. -> These operations do not automatically preserve injectivity.
- **anti-topological-opening-energy**: Charge the Sobolev energy of an opened carrier to the cubical cutoff estimate alone. -> Opening the collapsed fibres is a topological assertion without the claimed energy bound.
- **anti-circular-guard-capacities**: Select guards first and derive their required capacities from constants available only after the final realization. -> The barrier would depend on a capacity that was not fixed when its spacing was selected.
- **anti-uniform-inverse-snapping**: Use the snapping estimate as a uniform bound for its inverse or reverse the coordinate-change direction in a derivative estimate. -> The inverse bound may deteriorate with the fixed input configuration.
- **anti-unrestricted-edge-opening**: Preserve arbitrary new wall-edge tests automatically when opening the central carrier. -> Exact matching requires whole-wall avoidance of nonsingleton values, locally finite hit sets and the stated seam avoidance.
- **anti-subcritical-compression-outside-range**: Use marked-cube compression to absorb an uncontrolled interior energy in every exponent regime. -> The interior smallness mechanism depends on the subcritical exponent restriction.
- **anti-effective-finite-solver**: Advertise the existence proof as a finite numerical solver with a certified complexity or computable uniform distortion bound. -> The proof selects qualitative topological models and input-dependent constants before refining exceptional sets; it supplies no efficient dependence for those model bounds.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The selected result is existence of a strongly convergent sequence for arbitrary Sobolev homeomorphisms on open domains, rather than a finite input-output construction. The smoothing reduction selects qualitative PL model libraries and then refines the mesh after their bounds are fixed. At sm:model-derivative-bound the source states: "They may be arbitrarily large; no efficient dependence on $K_P$ is asserted." At stmt-hp-cutoff it also states: "This last assertion is topological; it does not assert a Sobolev energy bound for the opened maps." Finite numerical agreement cannot certify these global existence, topology and convergence assertions. An effective finite representation and certified model-selection procedure are ABSENT.

<a id="pm-s6"></a>
## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-main-domain-and-exponent** (hypothesis): The main approximation theorem requires bounded domains in three dimensions, a finite exponent strictly above two, and an input that is already a Sobolev homeomorphism. Blocked use: ['Applying the main theorem to unbounded domains.', 'Treating an arbitrary Sobolev map or sampled deformation as a certified homeomorphism.', 'Extending this range construction to the complementary exponent regime.']
- **limit-boundary-trace-prescription** (formal_scope): Smoothness is asserted on the open domains. The main result does not provide a boundary extension or preservation of prescribed boundary traces. Blocked use: ['Claiming boundary smoothness or exact boundary interpolation from the fixed-target conclusion.']
- **limit-forward-convergence-only** (formal_scope): Strong forward Sobolev convergence does not establish inverse Sobolev convergence or convergence of elastic energies with singular determinant penalties. Blocked use: ['Passing to a limit in inverse derivative energies.', 'Claiming convergence of a singular determinant penalty from forward strong convergence alone.']
- **limit-dimensional-extension** (counterexample_scope): The three-dimensional conclusion cannot be extended indiscriminately to higher dimensions. The cited higher-dimensional counterexamples concern their explicitly restricted exponent range. Blocked use: ['Advertising a dimension-independent density theorem.', 'Using the cited counterexamples to decide every higher-dimensional exponent regime.']
- **limit-naive-injective-approximation** (approximation): Ordinary convolution and fine vertex interpolation do not automatically preserve injectivity. Blocked use: ['Replacing the geometric construction by ordinary smoothing or vertex interpolation without a separate injectivity argument.']
- **limit-null-image-versus-source-energy** (edge_case): A deficient-rank image having zero target volume does not make the derivative energy on its source preimage negligible. Blocked use: ['Discarding retained positive deficient ranks solely because their image is volume-null.']
- **limit-lusin-regime** (hypothesis): The asserted volume Lusin conclusion requires the stated higher-exponent regime. Exceptional source null sets can require separate treatment below that regime. Blocked use: ['Eliminating exceptional inverse assignments throughout the main exponent range by assuming volume Lusin regularity.']
- **limit-flattening-inverse-distortion** (approximation): Strict flattening maps have inverse bounds depending on the positive strictness parameter; those bounds are not uniform as the parameter tends to zero. Blocked use: ['Transferring a uniform inverse distortion estimate from strict flattenings to the collapsed limit.']
- **limit-qualitative-fibre-opening** (nonconstructive): Opening the cutoff fibres supplies a topological homeomorphism with fine value control, without a Sobolev energy bound for the opened maps. Blocked use: ['Charging arbitrary topological hole fillings directly to the cutoff shell-energy estimate.']
- **limit-carrier-choice-order** (hypothesis): Endpoint exact regions and their buffers must be fixed before residual-volume thresholds are prescribed. Marked-collar enlargement factors precede the facet budgets. Blocked use: ['Reversing the carrier rounds or choosing an enlargement factor after its facet budgets have been paid.']
- **limit-regular-implantation-tests** (hypothesis): Regular affine implantation assumes bounded jets and inverse jets together with uniform differentiation tests. Independence of the final energy constant from condition numbers does not remove these prerequisites. Blocked use: ['Implanting exact affine cores at arbitrary full-rank points without the required uniform value and power-mean tests.']
- **limit-low-region-carrier-cost** (approximation): The central carrier modification has finite local Sobolev budgets, without a uniform bound for its new low-region costs. The subsequent construction confines active derivatives to the high-budget region. Blocked use: ['Applying the ordinary weak derivative estimate indiscriminately inside the modified low region.']
- **limit-sampled-edge-opening** (hypothesis): Exact edge matching requires whole-wall avoidance of nonsingleton values, finite hit sets on compact localizations, and the specified avoidance of nonexact seams. Blocked use: ['Assuming arbitrary newly introduced closed wall tests retain their exact edge intersections under opening.']
- **limit-prestack-contract-is-separate** (hypothesis): Independent product charts for individual collars do not supply the simultaneous pre-stack contract. Its qualitative requirements also do not provide an integral slope budget. Blocked use: ['Inferring compatible opposite-parameter trivializations from unrelated collar parametrizations.', 'Inferring guard-independent integral capacities from local Lipschitzness alone.']
- **limit-prior-capacities-and-realization** (hypothesis): Wall realization is conditional on the full geometric pre-stack contract, guard avoidance, ordered sampling data and capacities fixed before guards and final resolution. Blocked use: ['Applying conditional realization before supplying the actual pre-stacks and their prior integral bounds.', 'Absorbing an earlier energy tail using a constant selected only after the realization.']
- **limit-routing-local-finiteness** (edge_case): Before confinement, a routed surface may have ends at infinity. The required local finiteness controls whole original parent collars, rather than only the routed fragments. Blocked use: ['Treating every initially routed surface as compact.', 'Truncating and capping a routing tree using only fragment-based local finiteness.']
- **limit-no-ambient-realization-gradient-bound** (formal_scope): The exterior energy argument controls active scalar parameter differentials and target reconstruction speeds. It does not supply a quantitative bound for the derivative of the qualitative ambient realization. Blocked use: ['Substituting an uncontrolled ambient extension derivative into the principal energy estimate.']
- **limit-normalization-one-colour** (formal_scope): Individual edge-count preservation under normalization concerns one colour at a time and does not preserve the other colour automatically. Blocked use: ['Assuming separate normalizations already provide simultaneous opposite-colour product geometry.']
- **limit-snapping-direction-and-protection** (hypothesis): Snapping requires disjoint canonical and protected subcomplexes and quantitative bounds on the remaining cells. Uniform Lipschitz control is directed from new coordinates to old coordinates; inverse bounds may depend on the configuration. Blocked use: ['Reversing the snapping map in a uniform derivative estimate.', 'Prescribing unchanged protected traces that intersect the canonical subcomplex.', 'Ignoring quantitative buffer-cell parameter bounds.']
- **limit-sharp-estimate-localization** (approximation): Sharp scalar estimates apply in the protected clean geometry and compatible smooth label sectors, away from active central cutoffs. Nonregular, leakage and dirty regions require separate cost accounting. Blocked use: ['Applying the sharp clean-region bound on unrelated sectors or central activation transitions.', 'Replacing the full derivative cost of uncontrolled tetrahedra by a small-volume assertion.']
- **limit-subcritical-marked-compression** (hypothesis): Marked-interior compression requires an exponent strictly between two and three and a weighted collar-energy bound. Its smallness mechanism does not extend automatically to other exponents. Blocked use: ['Compressing an uncontrolled interior without verifying the collar-energy hypothesis.', 'Using the subcritical compression mechanism in the higher-exponent regime.']
- **limit-full-rank-correction-pretests** (hypothesis): The postponed affine correction needs previously selected full-rank cubes, fine preliminary value tests and small derivative energy on their buffered bands. Blocked use: ['Correcting an arbitrary preliminary homeomorphism without reserving the required value and band-energy tests.']
- **limit-smoothing-global-membership** (hypothesis): The smoothing theorem assumes global Sobolev membership as well as local bi-Lipschitzness. Local regularity alone does not establish finite total derivative energy. Blocked use: ['Invoking strong global smoothing before paying the marked-interior and residual energy costs.']
- **limit-qualitative-library-effectivity** (nonconstructive): Finite normalized model libraries provide finite local derivative bounds before exceptional sets are refined, without an asserted efficient dependence on local bi-Lipschitz constants. A finite numerical solver contract is ABSENT. Blocked use: ['Advertising a terminating numerical approximation algorithm or certified runtime from the existence proof.', 'Choosing the exceptional-set error before fixing the model constants that multiply it.']

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


We resolve the three-dimensional Ball–Evans approximation problem for every finite <i>p</i> &gt; 2. Every $`W^{1,p}`$ homeomorphism between arbitrary bounded domains in ℝ<sup>3</sup> can be approximated strongly in $`W^{1,p}`$ by smooth diffeomorphisms onto the same target.
